Title: Manjung council seizes 17 fighting cocks from house
Article:
LUMUT: Seventeen chickens believed to be used for cockfighting were seized from a house in Resident 3, Bandar Baru Setia Awan Perdana (BBSAP), here, yesterday.
Manjung Municipal Council (MPM) Licensing and Enforcement Department director Mohamad Sharil Salihan said the council had previously issued a notice ordering the homeowner to clean up the premises.
"A notice was also issued for the homeowner to stop keeping chickens that were causing a nuisance.
"However, the homeowner failed to comply with the instructions. MPM therefore took enforcement action and seized the chickens believed to have been used for cockfighting," he said here today.
He said two round cages and one square cage were also seized during the operation.
He said the seizure was intended to ensure that animals kept in residential areas did not cause a nuisance or breach regulations.
He did not rule out the possibility that the house had been illegally occupied by irresponsible individuals without the owner's knowledge.
"The chicken owner may have been renting the house. No one was present when MPM carried out the seizure.
"MPM will continue its monitoring and enforcement efforts to ensure residential areas remain clean, orderly and comfortable for all," he said.

Title: Fadhlina: 691 teachers need immediate psychological intervention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 691 teachers need immediate psychological interventions following a nationwide screening of 82,126 educators by the Education Ministry.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the Psychological Well-Being Inventory (IKPsi) findings showed 636 teachers were at a moderate level, 32 at a moderately low level, and 23 at a low level.
She said the group accounted for 0.84 per cent of the total number of teachers screened.
However, she said the vast majority, or 99.16 per cent, recorded good psychological well-being, comprising 50,869 teachers at a high level and 30,566 at a moderately high level.
"Overall, these findings show that the majority of teachers who underwent screening are at a good level of psychological well-being, but the ministry will continue to provide attention and intervention to teachers identified as needing support.
"To assist teachers facing these challenges, the ministry implements a comprehensive intervention approach covering developmental, preventive, and rehabilitative aspects through psychological and counselling services.
"Among the services provided are individual and group counselling, psychological testing, guidance and consultation, as well as stress management programmes and emotional support for ministry personnel," she said in a written reply published on the parliament website.
She was responding to a question from Datuk Muslimin Yahya (PN-Sungai Besar) on the number of teachers facing health problems and mental disorders, as well as the intervention measures and support assistance provided by the ministry to help them sustain their lives and careers.
Fadhlina said the intervention approach begins with screening and identifying individual needs, followed by suitable psychological and counselling interventions.
"Among the intervention measures implemented are those focusing on individual issues and needs, covering financial management, serious indebtedness, moderate performance, and mental health-related issues.
"In crises, the support provided through intervention can help individuals stabilise their emotions, identify strengths and support resources, and develop an action plan to restore functioning.
"The ministry's approach not only focuses on resolving current issues, but also strengthens the capacity of teachers to maintain long-term well-being. This effort aims to help teachers regain stability and function well, enabling them to pursue their lives and careers more resiliently," she said.
Apart from psychological and counselling interventions, the ministry is also upgrading staffrooms with a total allocation of RM200 million, including an additional RM100 million, to support educators' welfare.
"This initiative aims to provide more comfortable workspaces, improved basic amenities, and a conducive, professional atmosphere to support teachers' needs in performing their daily duties.
"Providing a suitable work environment not only improves the comfort and convenience of teachers, but also supports their physical, emotional, and psychological well-being in carrying out their responsibilities effectively.
"This effort aligns with the ministry's comprehensive approach to teachers' well-being, including preparing a work environment that fosters a positive, harmonious work atmosphere and supports their productivity and motivation," she said.
Fadhlina said the ministry would continue to strengthen psychological and counselling services, and roll out appropriate interventions based on the needs of education personnel to safeguard teachers' psychological well-being continuously.

Title: Petroleum subsidies projected to hit RM40bil this year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's petroleum subsidy bill is projected to reach RM40 billion this year as a global supply crisis pushes crude oil prices above US$120 per barrel.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said monthly subsidies for petrol, diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) surged from about RM800 million in January and February to nearly RM5 billion in March and April.
However, the monthly subsidy burden eased to about RM3 billion between June and August.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government had adopted a balanced approach to protect Malaysians from rising fuel prices while safeguarding the country's fiscal sustainability.
"The government has reprioritised its annual expenditure to focus on programmes that deliver the greatest impact to the people and the economy.
"This exercise takes into account the operational needs and priorities of each ministry, particularly to ensure that high-impact programmes and essential services, including education, healthcare and financial assistance, remain protected," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
He was responding to Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal (Warisan-Semporna), who sought details on petroleum subsidies.
Anwar said the government would strengthen fiscal discipline by tightening operating expenditure, improving public spending efficiency and reducing leakages in the implementation of programmes and subsidies.
"Enforcement activities have also been stepped up to ensure government assistance and subsidies reach those who are genuinely eligible, thereby optimising the use of public funds.
"The government will continue to balance the need to protect Malaysians from rising fuel prices with prudent expenditure management to ensure higher subsidy costs can be absorbed without compromising the country's fiscal sustainability," he added.

Title: Singapore, Indonesia leaders hold high-level talks amid bilateral challenges
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto have held high-level talks amid recent bilateral challenges.
Singapore Foreign Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan said the communication had established political commitment on both sides to do "what is necessary", and that the focus was now on implementing and executing the plans and commitments.
"I am not at liberty to discuss the details, but just let me give you the assurance that communication has occurred at the highest level between my prime minister and with President Prabowo," he told Singapore media following the conclusion of his working visit to Indonesia on Wednesday.
He was asked about the state of bilateral relations between Singapore and Indonesia following recent developments, as well as details of his meeting with Prabowo on the same day. The transcript of the interview was made available by Singapore's Foreign Ministry.
Balakrishnan described his visit to Jakarta as involving engagement at the highest level, having met his newly appointed Indonesian counterpart, Arrmanatha Nasir, and called on Prabowo.
"We had good conversations, honest conversations, sincere conversations, and we have come up with a few constructive approaches, some of which we are in the midst of implementing."
Balakrishnan said their announcement on Tuesday on the Joint Task Force "is a recognition that in the case of haze, it is a transboundary problem and it requires a collegiate, collective response on the part of both Indonesia and Singapore".
The minister said the task force aimed to facilitate a collective response, enhance information sharing and strengthen coordination to deter companies engaging in such anti-social and, frankly, dangerous acts.
"We can also hold them accountable, and we can try our best to make sure that this does not recur," he added.

Title: New bridge to end Pulau Bruit's ferry dependence, ushering in economic revival
Article:
SIBU: The new Batang Paloh Bridge, a RM289.8 million project opening tomorrow, will end Pulau Bruit, Daro's reliance on ferries and mark a new chapter in the island's economic growth.
The 1.7-kilometre bridge is expected to speed up the movement of residents and the transport of agricultural and marine produce to outside markets, easing the logistical constraints that have long hampered the island's economic activity.
Deputy Premier of Sarawak and Minister of Infrastructure and Port Development Sarawak Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas announced the bridge's opening at a recent sitting of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly.
He said the Batang Paloh Bridge, together with the completed Muara Lassa Bridge, will strengthen the coastal road network and enhance Pulau Bruit's connectivity with Daro, Tanjung Manis, Sarikei and surrounding areas.
A Bernama survey found that residents welcome the bridge's opening, expected to end the hardship of waiting for ferries, especially during festive seasons and school holidays, when waits can stretch to several hours.
Kampung Semop resident Salleh Jamain, 53, said the bridge's opening is highly anticipated, as it would not only ease travel to Sibu and Sarikei but also potentially boost his income through the vehicle-repair service he runs on the side.
"I was very happy when I learnt the bridge would open at the end of the month, because trips to town will become faster and easier.
"I also did not want to miss the chance to witness this historic moment," he told Bernama.
Salleh hopes the facility will invigorate local economic activity, opening up more job opportunities and sources of income for residents.
For smallholder oil palm farmers, the bridge's opening brings even greater benefits, as deliveries of their produce to markets outside the island will no longer be subject to ferry operating schedules.
Smallholder Omarmayah Rosli said he uses four pickup trucks a day to deliver oil palm fruit to buyers in Sarikei, but the number of trips depends on ferry services.
"Right now, the number of trips is rather limited because we depend on the ferry. Once the bridge opens, we can deliver oil palm fruit at any time and make more trips.
"This will not only boost the income of smallholders but also that of workers and vehicle owners transporting the oil palm harvest," he said.
Meanwhile, Kampung Semop community chief Kamri Haron described the bridge's opening as a key turning point in Pulau Bruit's development, particularly in widening market access for agricultural and fishery produce and stimulating local business activity.
"This bridge does not merely connect Pulau Bruit to the outside world but is also a symbol of progress that opens up more economic opportunities for residents," he said. — BERNAMA

Title: Adam Adli: PH, Bersatu may clash in Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan has not ruled out clashes with Bersatu in the Melaka election, despite an understanding between the two sides.
Melaka PKR acting state chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said clashes could occur in seats beyond the seven PH has decided not to contest.
Adam Adli, who is also PKR communications director, said the coalition's decision to contest only 21 of the 28 state legislative assembly seats did not mean it deliberately vacated the remaining seven to make way for Bersatu.
"When Bersatu expressed its intention to contest in Melaka, there could be clashes between PH and the party. We decided to contest 21 seats because that matches our current capability.
"We do not want to send the wrong message, as if we deliberately vacated the seven seats for Bersatu, but it is up to them. In fact, if there are overlapping seats between PH and Bersatu, there is no problem.
"I personally expect clashes, but if Bersatu wants to play safe, they can just take those seven seats," he said in an interview with Berita Harian.
Earlier, PH announced it would contest 21 seats in the Melaka election, with PKR fielding candidates in nine seats, DAP in seven, and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) in five.
PKR's nine state seats are Tanjung Bidara, Rembia, Asahan, Paya Rumput, Kelebang, Machap Jaya, Ayer Molek, Rim, and Serkam. DAP will contest Ayer Keroh, Kesidang, Kota Laksamana, Banda Hilir, Gadek, Duyong, and Pengkalan Batu, while Amanah will contest Kuala Linggi, Durian Tunggal, Bukit Katil, Telok Mas, and Merlimau.
The seven seats not contested by PH are Ayer Limau, Lendu, Taboh Naning, Sungai Udang, Pantai Kundor, Duyong, and Bemban.
Adam Adli, who is also the Deputy Higher Education Minister, said PH's decision to contest only 21 seats was not influenced by external parties or an electoral pact, as previously speculated.
He said Bersatu remained free to determine how many seats it wanted to contest, as no electoral pact had been established between both parties.
He said that if PH contested a seat and Bersatu also decided to field a candidate there, it was up to the party in the spirit of democracy.
"For these remaining seven seats, we do not have an electoral pact. We merely asked each other if there were seats they wished to contest. For PH, the principle is simple: no seat should go uncontested.
"That means no candidate should win uncontested. Otherwise, we disrupt the entire electoral process in this state election," he said.
He said it was crucial for every state seat to see at least a straight fight to give voters an opportunity to make a choice.
Meanwhile, a Bersatu source also indicated the possibility of seat clashes with PH, but declined to elaborate.

Title: CTOS faces weaker Q4 earnings on cyber disruption, higher taxes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd is expected to report weaker fourth-quarter earnings as cybersecurity-related service disruptions and higher tax expenses weigh on profitability, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
Analyst Mohd Shanaz Noor Azam said the temporary suspension of selected credit reporting services following the incident in late September could affect about 35 per cent of the company's revenue.
The disruption is expected to result in revenue losses and additional remediation costs, while transaction volumes could take 30 to 60 days to fully recover once services resume.
Shanaz said the expiry of CTOS's tax incentive on Nov 8 would add to earnings pressure, with taxable income becoming subject to the statutory corporate tax rate of 24 per cent.
This compares with the company's effective tax rate of 8.4 per cent in the first nine months of 2026.
"We expect these factors to weigh on fourth-quarter profitability, with the full impact of the higher tax rate becoming more pronounced in financial year 2027 (FY27)," he said in a note.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Hold" call on CTOS with a target price of 55 sen, pending the company's analyst briefing today.
The briefing is expected to provide greater clarity on the restoration of affected services and the recovery in transaction volumes.
Shanaz noted that CTOS had initially targeted resuming services in the third week of October, with each additional week of disruption potentially reducing profit after tax and minority interests by RM1.3 million.
He cautioned that prolonged disruptions could lead to customer losses, higher cybersecurity costs and further earnings pressure.
CIMB Securities said the successful restoration of affected services and a recovery in transaction volumes would be key catalysts for a potential re-rating of CTOS shares.
Other potential catalysts include stronger adoption of digital and alternative credit scoring solutions, cross-selling opportunities in Southeast Asia and possible special dividends from non-core asset disposals.
However, downside risks remain, including prolonged disruptions to Central Credit Reference Information System-related services, customers switching to competing credit bureaus and higher cybersecurity and compliance costs.
Other risks include slower sales conversion in the financial institution and corporate segment, further data breaches and adverse regulatory developments.

Title: PN banks on local, professional candidates for Melaka polls
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional is confident that its candidates for the Melaka election, scheduled to be announced tonight, can secure voters' support.
PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the line-up comprises individuals from diverse backgrounds, including locals and professionals who are active in community work.
"The candidates that PN will field are local figures and professionals who are heavily involved in community activities.
"They are also well known. God willing, our candidates will gain the support of voters in Melaka," he said when contacted.
Commenting on which party will contest the most state legislative assembly seats, Tuan Ibrahim said the matter would only be confirmed after the official announcement.
"Let us wait for tonight's announcement regarding the breakdown of parties and seats," he said.
It was previously reported that Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had confirmed seat negotiations with Pas for the Melaka election had been finalised.
Under the arrangement, BN confirmed it would contest 21 state seats, while Pas and its allies would contest seven.

Title: Malaysia faces population decline as fertility rate continues to fall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's total fertility rate (TFR) remains below the replacement level, recording 1.6 children per woman aged 15 to 49 in 2024.
National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN) director-general Datuk Abdul Shukur Abdullah said the rate was well below the population replacement level of 2.1 children per woman.
"Based on the Vital Statistics Malaysia 2025 report published by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), Malaysia's TFR for 2024 stood at 1.6 children for every woman aged 15 to 49.
"This rate is far below the population replacement level, which is around 2.1 children per woman," he said.
By ethnic group, the Malay community recorded the highest TFR in 2024 at 1.9 children per woman, followed by other Bumiputeras at 1.6, Indians at 1.1, and Chinese at 0.9.
He said that while the Chinese community recorded the lowest fertility rate, the trend should not be linked solely to cultural or racial factors.
"Among the factors influencing low fertility are delayed marriages, an increasing age when having the first child, living and housing costs, childcare and education expenses, higher female participation in education and employment, and challenges in balancing work and family responsibilities," he said.
He said couples in urban areas were also more cautious about family planning.
"The decision to have a second or third child does not depend merely on the desire to have children, but on whether the family has sufficient time, financial resources, childcare support, and workplace backing," he said.
He said Malaysia must intensify interventions to slow the declining fertility rate to prevent population decline and age-structure imbalances by 2100.
Abdul Shukur said the national TFR dropped from 2.0 children per woman in 2015 to 1.6 in 2024.
The drop was far below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman, which is the level needed to maintain population size over the long term without taking migration into account, he said.
"However, declining fertility is not unique to Malaysia. It is a global trend, especially in developed countries where more women pursue higher education, enter the workforce, and postpone marriage and childbearing.
"Malaysia is among the countries experiencing a rapid decline in fertility rates. Looking at the data from 2015 to 2024, the rate fell by 0.4 points in about 10 years.
"Therefore, interventions must be carried out to slow this trend so that we can delay population decline," he said.
On long-term targets, Abdul Shukur said demographic studies showed Malaysia was unlikely to meet its previously projected target of 70 million people by 2100.
He said Malaysia must address changes in its population structure caused by declining birth rates and rising life expectancy.
"This situation can lead to an increase in the elderly population compared with the youth, which will strain social support systems, healthcare, and retirement savings.
"With the fertility rate at 1.6, we must look at the long-term impact.
"If births continue to fall behind deaths, the population could begin to shrink," he said.
On efforts to boost fertility rates, Abdul Shukur said it was not an easy task as it required substantial investment and a comprehensive approach to ease the cost of raising children.
"The experience of several countries that have succeeded in raising fertility rates shows that governments must provide financial support and facilities that enable couples to balance work and family life.
"The government needs to invest in reducing the cost of raising children, including financial aid, childcare, and family support.
"When couples are forced to choose between building careers and having children, costs and support facilities become key considerations," he said.
He noted that several states had introduced childbirth and family-related assistance, but their capacity to offer incentives varied depending on their financial standing.
"Therefore, efforts to raise fertility cannot rely solely on baby bonuses. They must be supported by a family-friendly ecosystem that encompasses childcare, education, and work-life balance," he said.
Abdul Shukur also said preparations for an ageing population must be prioritised, including ensuring that senior citizens have adequate retirement savings and strong family support systems.
He said longer life expectancy meant people must prepare financially and physically for extended retirement years.
"Ageing is not just about population figures. We must also look at physical and mental health, financial capacity, and family support.
"Family ties are essential so that the elderly are not marginalised or forced to live alone without support," he said.
Abdul Shukur added that strong family foundations must be established before marriage and maintained throughout family life to foster love, responsibility, and mutual support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Magnitude 5.5 quake hits Japan's Chiba Prefecture
Article:
TOKYO: An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.5 struck the northeastern part of Chiba Prefecture, near Tokyo, early Thursday, Kyodo News reported, citing the country's weather agency.
The quake, which occurred at 12.07am local time and measured lower 5 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, originated at a depth of about 52 kilometres and posed no tsunami threat, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.
A lower 5 reading was recorded in Yokoshibahikari, while weaker shaking was registered in other parts of the prefecture. The quake was also felt in Tokyo and neighbouring prefectures, including Tochigi, Ibaraki and Saitama.
The agency initially reported the quake's magnitude as 5.4 and estimated that it had occurred at a depth of about 50km.

Title: PM Anwar expresses deep sadness over the tragic train collision in Spain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed deep grief over the tragic loss of lives in the train collision in Spain.
In a Facebook post, he said Malaysia stood in solidarity with the people of Spain at this difficult time.
"Our thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones, and we wish the injured a swift recovery," he said.
Anwar also paid tribute to the emergency personnel and others working tirelessly at the scene.
"On behalf of the government and people of Malaysia, I extend our deepest condolences to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, the government and people of Spain, and especially to the families of the victims," Prime Minister said.
Yesterday, media reports said the death toll from Wednesday's high-speed train collision in central Spain has more than doubled to at least 64 people, according to the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha, making it even deadlier than a devastating rail accident near Adamuz in January.
However, the Malaysian Embassy in Madrid has yet to receive confirmation of any Malaysians affected by the collision involving two high-speed passenger trains.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersih questions Loke's RM1,000 taxi aid announcement ahead of Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Coalition for Clean and Fair Elections (Bersih) has criticised Transport Minister Anthony Loke for announcing a RM1,000 special financial assistance for taxi drivers during a Pakatan Harapan candidate announcement event for the Melaka election.
The Bersih steering committee said the move could create the perception that the aid was a contribution from a contesting party, even though it was funded by government revenue.
It said government-funded assistance should not be announced or promoted at political campaign events, as it could provide an unfair advantage to the ruling party.
"Proceeds from the sale of special registration numbers used to fund this aid are government revenue that should rightfully benefit all citizens.
"It is not money belonging to any political party and should not be announced or promoted during campaign events to give an advantage to the ruling party," Bersih said in a statement.
Bersih said explanations that the assistance was meant for recipients nationwide did not address why the aid for Melaka drivers was highlighted during the PH candidate announcement ceremony.
Loke had previously denied that the RM1,000 special aid for taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers in Melaka was aimed at fishing for votes in the state polls.
He said the incentive was being provided to all taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers nationwide, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of the 2027 Budget in parliament recently.S
The aid is funded by proceeds from the sale of the special "H" vehicle registration numbers, which recorded a total collection of RM91.21 million.
Revenue from the sales was channelled into several public initiatives, including the MyLesen Programme, free motorcycle helmets, and financial assistance for taxi and rental car drivers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI literacy, BRICS participation among focus of Dewan Rakyat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry's plans to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) literacy into the school curriculum, Malaysia's participation as a BRICS partner country and the drafting of an AI Governance Bill are among the key topics to be addressed in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on the Parliament website, during Ministers' Question Time, Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (PN-Merbok) will ask the Education Minister to outline the ministry's plans to incorporate AI literacy into the school curriculum through the AI Literacy Guide.
The proceedings will then continue with a question-and-answer session, during which Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) will ask the Foreign Affairs Minister to explain the objectives of Malaysia's participation as a BRICS partner country and the added value it offers compared with existing bilateral cooperation.
Additionally, Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) will ask the Digital Minister about the status of the drafting of the AI Governance Bill, the expected timeline for its tabling in the Dewan Rakyat and the existing legal protections available to citizens who fall victim to fraud.
Datuk Seri Doris Sophia anak Brodi (GPS-Sri Aman) will ask the Foreign Affairs Minister to provide the number of Malaysians detained or charged with drug-related offences abroad over the past five years, as well as comment on the effectiveness of airport scanning technology in detecting drugs and the current state of security.
During the same session, Datuk Seri Sh Mohmed Puzi Sh Ali (BN-Pekan) will ask the Agriculture and Food Security Minister for statistics on the economic returns generated by the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Show (MAHA) and the extent to which the event has benefited small-scale operators.
The winding-up session for the debate on the Supply Bill 2027, scheduled for tomorrow, will involve several ministries, including the Plantation and Commodities Ministry, the Communications Ministry, the Human Resources Ministry, the Economy Ministry, the Youth and Sports Ministry and the Finance Ministry, before the Dewan Rakyat proceeds to vote on the Bill.

Title: Jawi introduces multi-tier graves to optimise cemetery space [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Territory Islamic Religious Department (Jawi) has introduced tiered burials at the Raudhatul Sakinah Islamic Cemetery in Kepong to optimise limited burial space.
The pilot project is being implemented by the department's Mosque Management Division in collaboration with the Dakwah Management Division and the Kuala Lumpur Public Works Department (PWD), specifically for unclaimed bodies.
Jawi said the initiative also introduces a pulley machine developed by Kuala Lumpur PWD to lower bodies to a depth of eight feet.
"In addition, to ensure structural safety, trench boxes are used to prevent soil collapse during the tiered burial process," Jawi said in a statement.
The department hopes the equipment will improve burial efficiency and assist ground personnel.
"Efforts to improve and upgrade the operations of Islamic cemeteries, including exploring suitable technologies and equipment, aim to ensure Jawi's services are delivered effectively.
"This effort also reflects the department's commitment to ensuring funeral management is carried out responsibly, orderly and respectfully in accordance with Islamic requirements," it said.

Title: Perak SADC prioritises staff wellness
Article:
IPOH:  Perak State Agricultural Development Corp (Perak SADC) has strengthened its workplace health culture through the Perak SADC Active & Wellness Day 2026 programme.
The event brought together 250 employees from the corporation's headquarters and plantations under its management.
[[nid:1565955]]
It aimed to encourage an active lifestyle and highlight the importance of work-life balance in creating a healthier and more productive working environment.
Perak SADC chief executive officer Mohd Azhar Mohd Yusof said untreated health problems could affect employees' ability to perform their duties effectively and, in turn, impact organisational productivity.
"Sometimes, we see even young employees facing health problems. That is why we want to cultivate a culture of looking after our health so they can work well and achieve high performance.
"If our mental and physical health is not strong, how can we work towards high performance?" he said.
Azhar  was speaking at the programme, themed "Active Together, Well Together", at Dewan Kelarai, Serai Estate, here yesterday.
The programme featured a 5km run and fun walk, free comprehensive health screenings and knowledge-sharing sessions on work-life balance, healthy eating and personal healthcare.
[[nid:1565954]]
Free screening services included  blood pressure monitoring, blood sugar and cholesterol checks, eye examinations, bone density tests, Smart Pulse assessments, body composition analysis and consultations.
The programme also featured interactive quizzes, lucky draws and a blood donation drive in collaboration with  Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital.
Azhar said the event received sponsorship and support from the Health Ministry, HTM Pharmacy, Quill Ipoh Orthopaedic Hospital, Sunway Medical Centre Ipoh, Decathlon, Takaful Malaysia, ViQ and Serai Group.
Held in conjunction with National Sports Day, the programme provided an opportunity to boost ties between headquarters staff and employees at Perak SADC-managed plantations across the state.
"It gives plantation management staff an opportunity to interact with senior officers at headquarters. They can also undergo  health screenings and donate blood."
Azhar said Perak SADC planned to organise more recreational activities next year to promote healthy living, including hiking and rafting.
"These activities are aimed at safeguarding the health of Perak SADC employees while boosting  relationships among colleagues through group recreation."
In a related development, Azhar said the corporation's commitment to employee welfare had been recognised through two awards.
These were the HR Sustainability & Transformation Award 2026 at the Asean HR Excellence Awards 2026 (Malaysia Edition) and the Perak Best Employer Award 2026 from the Employees Provident Fund.
"These awards show that we prioritise employee welfare. Human resources are our most valuable asset because our people are the ones who drive the organisation towards excellence," he said. By Muhammad Zulsyamini Sufian Suri
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar on expectations of OPR normalisation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by the possibility of overnight policy rate (OPR) normalisation at Bank Negara Malaysia Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting next week.
At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0720/0800 against the US dollar from Wednesday's close of 4.0745/0790.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the unchanged OPR at 2.75 per cent could provide support for the local currency.
Meanwhile, he said the US dollar index (DXY) is currently down by 0.19 per cent to 102.127 points as Federal Open Market Committee members left the benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75 per cent to four per cent.
"It appears that the Federal Reserve is taking a guarded approach to reach its price stability goal at a time when the economy is deemed to be growing at a robust rate.
"On that note, we foresee the ringgit could be well supported," he told Bernama.
At the open, the ringgit was traded mostly lower against major currencies.
The ringgit gained vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5798/5851 from 2.5812/5843 at Wednesday's close, but edged down against the British pound to 5.4268/4374 from 5.4130/4190 and fell against the euro to 4.5427/5516 from 4.5337/5387.
The ringgit performed mixed against its Asean peers.
It inched up against the Indonesian rupiah to 223.9/224.4 from 224.0/224.4, while flat against the Philippine peso at 6.36/6.37.
The local note fell against the Singapore dollar to 3.1785/1850 from 3.1775/1813 at Wednesday's close, and was marginally lower against the Thai baht to 12.0759/1068 from 12.0726/0902.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nike deepens India push with new running shoe, seeking fresh growth engines
Article:
NEW YORK: Nike unveiled on Wednesday its first-ever running shoe designed specifically for India, marking the sportswear giant's latest bid to reach shoppers in the world's most populous country as it grapples with a sales slump in other key regions including China.
The shoe, dubbed Vegam Run, follows Nike's announcement earlier this month that it plans to open a new campus in India, where it is seeking to make inroads amid a running boom.
The running shoe is set to be released on India's e-commerce marketplace Flipkart on November 1, priced at ₹3,795 (RM163). It was developed in about five months, Nike said.
CEO Elliott Hill, two years into his tenure, is betting on a revamped product pipeline to turn around the struggling sportswear juggernaut, which analysts say will hinge in large part on locally led designs in key markets.
Nike is trying to push into India at a time when China, historically a profit driver for the company, continues to show particular weakness.
Sales in China, which account for about fifteen per cent of Nike's annual revenue, have fallen for nine consecutive quarters as international rivals ‌and domestic ⁠sportswear groups gain traction.
Shares have tumbled more than 40 per cent so far this year. But Nike's global running business has emerged as a bright spot, growing by double digits for six consecutive quarters.
"Our Nike performance business is not yet large enough to offset the pressure ​we're seeing in Nike sportswear, Jordan brand, and Greater China," Hill warned analysts this month after the company projected a surprisingly steep drop in full-year revenue. — REUTERS

Title: 25 tonnes of suspected Thai smuggled rice seized in Kelantan
Article:
GUA MUSANG: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 25 tonnes of white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand along Jalan Bentong-Kota Bharu near Paloh here on Tuesday night.
The seizure was made by the Southeast Brigade Commander's special team under Op Taring Wawasan after stopping a lorry at 11pm.
Southeast Brigade GOF commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said an inspection found that the lorry was carrying white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand.
"The lorry driver produced two copies of invoices to explain the source and destination of the rice consignment. However, there were doubts over the delivery location stated in the invoices.
"Following this, the 38-year-old driver was arrested, while the lorry and its 25,000kg rice cargo were seized for further action," he said in a statement.
Ahmad Radzi said the total value of the lorry and rice seized was estimated at RM550,000.
He said the modus operandi involved using suspected fake intermediary invoices to mislead the authorities during inspections and make the shipment appear to be supported by legitimate documents.
"Preliminary checks raised doubts over the delivery location stated in the invoices, as the location provided was inaccurate.
"This raised suspicions that the documents were being used to mislead the authorities about the actual source and destination of the rice consignment.
"Information obtained from the arrest will be further developed to identify the source of supply, those involved in preparing the documents, transporters, recipients and distribution network for the rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 20 of the Control of Padi and Rice Act 1994.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes kill five
Article:
GAZA CITY: Gaza's civil defence agency and a local hospital said Israeli strikes killed five people and wounded others in the Palestinian territory on Wednesday.
"Three people were killed and several others wounded, some of them seriously" in a drone attack in Rafah in the south, according to Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for the civil defence agency, a rescue force operating under Hamas authority.
The local hospital said it had received three bodies and 15 wounded people, one of whom later died from his injuries, according to Gaza's civil defence agency.
Gaza's civil defence agency said another person was killed in a strike in Khan Younis, also in the south.
Asked for comment by AFP, the Israeli army said "we struck terrorists in the area", adding that it would provide further information soon.
The strikes occurred a day after Israelis voted in a hard-fought election that produced no clear winner.
Since the ceasefire began last year, more than 1,500 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.
The war began on Oct 7, 2023, following an unprecedented attack by Hamas on southern Israel that killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
Israel responded with a massive military campaign that has destroyed much of Gaza and killed more than 74,500 people, according to the territory's health ministry.

Title: Early savings pave the way for a child's future
Article:
A CHILD'S future is full of possibilities. Many children start developing their ambitions and dreams young.
For parents, preparing for their children's future is not something that can be achieved overnight. It requires early planning and consistent effort, including setting aside savings for their education.
Through Bulan Menabung Simpan SSPN (BMS) 2026, the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) is highlighting the importance of saving as a key step parents can take to prepare for their children's education future.
BMS 2026 runs from Sept 25 to Nov 1, with the theme "Under the Sea". The campaign likens the savings journey to exploring the depths of the ocean, where countless wonders and possibilities await discovery.
The deeper one dives, the more there is to discover. Similarly, a child's journey through life presents numerous opportunities and possibilities.
Some children dream of becoming doctors, teachers, engineers, entrepreneurs or athletes, while others aspire to pursue creative careers.
Each dream comes with its own journey and education is one of the key foundations that can help prepare children for the future.
Every contribution to a child's savings is a small but meaningful step towards helping them achieve their ambitions.
Parents do not need to wait until they have accumulated a substantial amount before they start saving. What matters most is taking the first step early and developing a consistent saving habit.
When it comes to shaping children's future, parents can become real-life superheroes, always standing behind them, offering support and providing for their needs.
Saving for education is not merely about setting aside money. It also reflects parents' love, commitment and determination to secure a better future for their children.
[[nid:1565896]]
Although children may not yet understand the importance of savings, the efforts parents make from an early age can help prepare them for when they are ready to pursue further education.
Through the tagline "Jom Jadi Superhero Anak Anda!", BMS 2026 encourages parents to play their role in everyday life.
A superhero does not need to wear a costume or have extraordinary powers. To a child, a superhero can be a mother or father who is willing to plan ahead, make sacrifices and prepare for the future to give them the opportunity to pursue their dreams.
Preparing for a child's future can begin with one simple step today: saving.
Every contribution serves a purpose, every step carries meaning and every childhood dream deserves to be supported by careful preparation.
Through BMS 2026, parents are reminded that their children's future is not something they must wait to discover. Instead, they can begin exploring the possibilities today, one savings contribution at a time.
Parents are encouraged to take part in the BMS 2026 Closing Programme, which will be held from today to Sunday at the Centre Court, Alamanda Shopping Mall, Putrajaya.

Title: Wall Street ends higher as Fed holds key rate steady, focus turns to earnings
Article:
NEW YORK: US stock indexes advanced on Wednesday after the US Federal Reserve left its key policy rate unchanged, as widely expected, leaving investors betting on a rate hike at its next monetary policy meeting in December.
In its accompanying statement, the Fed upgraded its assessment of the economy while acknowledging inflation "remains elevated".
At the press conference following the release, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank had made clear its willingness and readiness to act.
"The Fed didn't throw any curveballs," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha. "It was widely expected they'd hold, so no big surprise there."
All three major US stock indexes oscillated following the decision and throughout Warsh's subsequent press conference, but ended the session higher.
"Market participants are getting more used to (Warsh's) style," Detrick added.
Financial markets are pricing in an 85.00 per cent likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's December meeting, up from 78.30 per cent on Tuesday, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Rate hike forecasts could be swayed by data expected on Thursday, including the Commerce Department's Personal Consumption Expenditures report — which includes the central bank's preferred inflation gauge — and an advance take on third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP).
Third-quarter earnings season is in full swing, with 200 companies in the S&P 500 having posted results. Of those, 84 per cent have beaten consensus estimates, according to the most recent LSEG data.
Analysts estimate aggregate third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.80 per cent year-on-year, up from 30.60 per cent as of Oct 1, per LSEG.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology jumped 5.90 per cent after South Korean rival SK Hynix reported a more than sevenfold jump in quarterly profit. SK Hynix's US-listed shares jumped 13.30 per cent.
The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index gained 1.80 per cent, notching its fourth consecutive daily advance and bouncing back from its recent sell-off.
"I think the market realises what the Fed did today is one thing, but are AI expenditures continuing?" Detrick said. "That's what the market's focused on."
Microsoft gained over four per cent in extended trading after posting quarterly results, while Alphabet shares dropped more than seven per cent in after-hours trading following the Google parent's earnings report.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 97.53 points, or 0.19 per cent, to 52,475.10, the S&P 500 gained 21.37 points, or 0.28 per cent, to 7,743.97 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 72.04 points, or 0.27 per cent, to 26,549.85.
US crude prices climbed after Iran-backed Houthis attacked a refinery in Saudi Arabia, adding to supply worries.
Since the Iran war began, oil prices have soared to over US$100 per barrel, pushing up costs in other areas of the economy and driving inflation higher.
Robinhood dipped 3.30 per cent after softness in cryptocurrencies dragged the trading platform's third-quarter profit below analyst expectations.
Vertiv surged 16.50 per cent after the digital infrastructure firm topped quarterly expectations and raised its full-year profit and revenue forecasts.
Boston Scientific dropped 5.80 per cent after the medical device maker trimmed its annual profit forecast.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.05-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 110 new highs and 214 new lows on the NYSE.
On the Nasdaq, 2,849 stocks rose and 1,926 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.48-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 19 new 52-week highs and 14 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 75 new highs and 198 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was 16.67 billion shares, compared with the 17.10 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

Title: Dollar falls after Fed holds rates steady
Article:
NEW YORK: The US dollar fell against major currencies on Wednesday after the Fed delivered a rate decision in line with expectations, while the New Zealand dollar fell sharply after that country's central bank surprised markets by leaving interest rates unchanged.
The Fed held interest rates steady, as expected, opting to delay any changes to borrowing costs until after next week's US midterm elections and awaiting further data on the path of inflation.
The dollar had a muted immediate reaction following the announcement of the Fed decision, but it began losing ground later as Chair Kevin Warsh spoke in a press briefing.
The euro was up 0.32 per cent against the dollar at US$1.1160. Against the Japanese yen, the dollar was down 0.04 per cent at 157.87 yen.
"The US dollar is softer than it was going into the FOMC as there's been a steepening in the yield curve," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex.
The Treasury yield curve steepened after Warsh started his press conference, with the two-year note yield, which typically moves in step with Fed interest rate expectations, falling 1.46 basis points to 4.72 per cent.
Markets are currently pricing in a nearly 85 per cent chance of a Fed rate hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six other currencies, was down 0.2 per cent at 102.15.
"This meeting landed right on target for what expectations were," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management.
"There wasn't much probability of a rate hike."
British finance minister John Healey told parliament on Wednesday he would raise taxes on banks, gambling and income for savers and landlords, while tightening value-added tax rules for online marketplaces such as Amazon, to fund the country's budget package.
The pound was up 0.12 per cent against the dollar at US$1.3323 and was down about 0.08 per cent versus the euro.
KIWI FALLS
The New Zealand dollar sank as much as 1.74 per cent to US$0.5583 after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand held interest rates at 2.75 per cent, surprising a large majority of economists who had expected a rate hike.
The Bank of Canada raised its key policy rate for the first time in more than three years and said further increases might be needed to prevent soaring energy costs from fuelling broader inflation.
The Canadian dollar strengthened 0.37 per cent versus the greenback to C$1.40 per dollar.
"The Reserve Bank of New Zealand disappointed markets and the New Zealand dollar sold off in response. It's the weakest of the G10 currencies. The Bank of Canada just hiked rates but it was expected. The Canadian dollar hasn't reacted much to the hike," Chandler said.
The European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan are expected to deliver monetary policy verdicts on Thursday and Friday, respectively, with both central banks expected to leave policy rates unchanged.

Title: Japan wants tougher action on cross-border threats
Article:
BANGI: Japan  called for stronger adherence to the rule of law and closer coordination among Asean countries to tackle cross-border threats, including maritime security challenges and transnational scam operations.
Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki said Japan wanted to work with Malaysia and other regional partners to uphold a free and open international order based on the rule of law.
Speaking at the Tuanku Chancellor International Conference on Law  2026, which was  attended by Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM)   chancellor Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and his two sons, Shikata said attempts to change the status quo by force or coercion in the South China Sea remained a regional concern.
He  added  that scam operations were spreading into Malaysia, with young Japanese allegedly recruited through deceptive job advertisements.
Japan had initially believed such operations were concentrated in Cambodia, Laos and Thailand, but they were now emerging in Malaysia, he said.
"This is something  we need to collaborate (on) with the legal authorities of both countries, including police."
He   stressed the importance of coordination among Malaysian agencies and said  Japan had worked with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime to bring nearly 10 Malaysian government agencies together to discuss the threat.
Japan was also strengthening maritime security ties with Malaysia, including support for the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and cooperation between the countries' coast guards.

Title: US Fed holds interest rates steady despite 'too high' inflation
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday held interest rates steady, even as its Chairman Kevin Warsh said inflation remained "too high" but insisted that politics played no part in the central bank's decision not to continue raising rates days before crucial midterm elections.
The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 to 4.00 per cent, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate quarter-point rate hike.
"Energy and related prices have moved higher again in recent weeks, and our job is to ensure that relative price changes in some sectors do not broaden out across the economy," Warsh told reporters.
Still, he said the FOMC needed more information in the coming weeks to "determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the two-per-cent goal."
The committee is scheduled to meet again in early December.
POLITICS PLAYED NO ROLE
The central bank has missed its inflation target for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.
US President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fuelled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies.
Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it.
The decision comes six days ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Trump's Republicans.
Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
US consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7 per cent, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
"Politics played no role in the decision," said Warsh, who has insisted that he supports the Fed's independence despite repeated attacks on the institution by Trump since he took office.
Speaking to broadcaster CNBC after the Fed's meeting, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he and Trump had "great confidence" in Warsh.
"I have great confidence in Chair Warsh to steer the Fed between the right combination of growth and inflation because what you don't want to do is cause enough of a growth slowdown that energy consumption would drop," he said.
STRONG' ECONOMIC GROWTH
On Wednesday, the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a "strong" pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.
At his press conference, Warsh spoke to that theme, and questioned whether the AI-led investment boom was fuelling inflation.
"Is the economy running too hot? Is the economy running too strong? That isn't the judgment of most of my colleagues," he said.
In a significant move, Warsh also announced that the Fed would be reducing the number of times it sets interest rates in the next two years.
It will continue to meet eight times a year in 2027 and 2028, but will only set interest rates seven times next year and six times the year after that.
"Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular, and information-rich intervals," said Warsh.
"But it's equally important we reserve time and space as an intellectually diverse group for strategic deliberations, for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons."
DON'T UNDERSTAND THE LOGIC
Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labour market — the Fed's other mandate — has been largely stable.
"In terms of the economics of it, I don't totally understand the logic," she said.
"If there was a reason to raise interest rates at the last meeting, I think that there's just as compelling of an economic reason to raise interest rates at this meeting."
The Fed has a dual mandate to maintain maximum employment while keeping inflation to its long-term target.
It achieves this goal largely using one tool: the economy's key interest rate. Raising rates tends to cool inflation but can also dampen economic activity; lowering them can spur economic activity but also fuel inflation.
The US unemployment rate has been largely stable around 4.2 per cent over the last year, with job growth mostly in positive territory — albeit driven by a few sectors.
Other advanced economies have also been grappling with high inflation, and on Wednesday Canada's central bank raised its key rate to 2.5 per cent, its first hike since July 2023.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Corporate reputation as a strategic priority
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Corporate reputation is one of an organisation's most valuable intangible assets. It reflects stakeholders' perceptions of the organisation's integrity, competence, reliability and commitment to responsible business practices. While a strong reputation may take decades to establish, it can be severely damaged within hours by a corporate scandal, unethical conduct, regulatory breach or misleading public statement. Safeguarding corporate reputation must therefore be a strategic priority for boards and senior management.
Understanding Reputation Risk
Reputation risk is the possibility that negative stakeholder perceptions will adversely affect an organisation's business operations, financial performance, market position or long-term sustainability. Stakeholders include shareholders, customers, employees, regulators, suppliers and the wider community.
Reputation risk often arises as a consequence of other risks. Financial mismanagement, fraud, corruption, poor product quality, cybersecurity incidents and environmental misconduct can all trigger reputational damage. For example, a data breach may result not only in financial losses and regulatory penalties but also in the loss of customer confidence. Reputation risk can therefore act as a risk multiplier, magnifying the consequences of an underlying failure.
Common Sources of Reputation Risk
Several factors threaten corporate reputation.
Unethical leadership and misconduct: Fraud, corruption, conflicts of interest and abuse of authority undermine confidence in management and the board. When senior leaders fail to uphold ethical standards, the organisation's credibility may suffer.
Regulatory non-compliance: Violations of applicable laws, regulations and governance requirements can lead to enforcement action, financial penalties and negative publicity.
Poor customer experience: Defective products, unsafe services, misleading advertising and unresolved complaints can damage customer loyalty and public confidence.
Cybersecurity and data breaches: Failure to protect confidential information raises questions about an organisation's competence and commitment to stakeholder interests.
Environmental and social irresponsibility: Pollution, unsafe working conditions and unsupported sustainability claims may expose organisations to public criticism and stakeholder distrust.
Safeguarding Corporate Reputation
Effective reputation risk management begins with prevention rather than crisis response.
First, the board and senior management must establish a strong ethical culture. Codes of conduct, anti-corruption policies and conflict-of-interest procedures must be supported by leadership that demonstrates integrity, accountability and transparency.
Second, reputation risk should be integrated into the enterprise risk management framework. Organisations should identify potential threats, assess their likelihood and impact, assign risk owners and establish appropriate controls. Assessments should consider financial consequences as well as potential damage to stakeholder trust.
Third, effective internal controls, compliance monitoring and independent oversight can help detect misconduct and operational weaknesses before they escalate. Confidential whistleblowing channels should encourage employees to report wrongdoing without fear of retaliation.
Fourth, organisations should monitor customer complaints, stakeholder feedback, media coverage and emerging issues. Early detection enables management to investigate concerns and take corrective action before reputational damage spreads.
Managing a Reputation Crisis
Despite preventive measures, crises may still occur. Organisations should respond promptly, establish the facts and communicate accurately with affected stakeholders. Concealing problems, making misleading statements or offering unsupported assurances can worsen the situation.
Where failures occur, management should acknowledge the problem, explain corrective actions and address the root causes. Following the crisis, a review should identify control weaknesses and implement measures to prevent recurrence.
The board oversees reputation risk as part of its governance responsibilities. Internal audit can provide independent assurance on the effectiveness of relevant governance, risk management and internal controls, including whistleblowing arrangements and crisis management procedures. Management, however, remains responsible for managing these risks.
Conclusion
Corporate reputation cannot be protected through public relations campaigns alone. It must be earned through ethical leadership, responsible decisions, effective governance and consistent conduct. Organisations that identify threats early, address failures transparently and learn from mistakes are better positioned to preserve stakeholder confidence.
Ultimately, reputation is not what an organisation says about itself but what stakeholders believe about it based on its actions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Data centres must secure water, power supply before approval [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Data centre investments must have adequate water and electricity supplies before they can receive federal government approval, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said the government would ensure that states have sufficient water supplies to support data centre developments without compromising the needs of other industries.
Speaking during his 2027 Budget wind-up speech in the Dewan Rakyat on Wednesday, Johari said investors were also encouraged to adopt water recycling technology.
"When it comes to water supply, we will ensure the state government is committed to securing sufficient water supply. If there is not enough water in the state, don't host data centres.
"As for the investors, we encourage them to bring their own technology to recycle the water used," he said.
Johari was responding to a supplementary question from Simpang Renggam Member of Parliament (MP) Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad on the agencies involved in approving data centre investments.
He said applications must go through the Malaysian Investment Development Authority, with decisions taking into account recommendations from the Data Centre Task Force (DCTF).
The task force comprises representatives from the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry, Digital Ministry and Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry.
State governments and water supply authorities are also involved in the discussions.
"At the federal government level, we assess electricity requirements, with detailed discussions involving Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
"Through the DCTF, we want to ensure there is sufficient electricity reserve capacity in these states, and supply is allocated only to data centres with access to it," he said.
Johari added that data centres unable to secure grid electricity supply would have to explore off-grid alternatives.
He said the government had approved 117 data centres nationwide, of which 55 were operational, 19 were under construction and 16 had received approval but had yet to begin development.
The remaining 27 projects were at various stages of development, including some that had yet to commence work. These projects would obtain electricity through off-grid sources, he said.
Separately, Johari backed a proposal to position the Lahad Datu Palm Oil Industrial Cluster (POIC) Industrial Park in Sabah as a key industrial and investment hub under the Brunei Darussalam–Indonesia–Malaysia–Philippines East Asean Growth Area (BIMP-EAGA) initiative.
He said the proposal was long overdue, adding that the POIC should have been developed ahead of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone.
"It could be a very strategic place because, first, there is land, and secondly, there are sufficient port facilities.
"I support the suggestion from the Penampang MP, and we could discuss ways to make the area a special economic zone," he said.
Johari was responding to Penampang MP Datuk Ewon Benedick, who proposed developing Sabah as Malaysia's "Eastern Gateway", with the Lahad Datu POIC serving as a key hub for industrial development and investment under BIMP-EAGA.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia must turn US$50bil AI investment into high-value jobs, technology gains [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must turn a proposed US$50 billion (RM204 billion) investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres by a global investor into higher-paying jobs, technology transfer and stronger local businesses, rather than simply expanding its digital infrastructure, economists say.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on Saturday that Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia had been identified as locations for the proposed investment.
The investment, potentially one of the largest of its kind in the region, presents an opportunity to accelerate Malaysia's digital economy, but its long-term value will depend on how much economic activity, expertise and income it generates domestically, economists said.
Nikkei Asia reported on Monday, citing a call between Anwar and SoftBank Group Corp founder Masayoshi Son last week, that the Japanese conglomerate was discussing participation in the investment plan focused on AI and data centres.
SoftBank is expected to contribute only part of the proposed amount, with project financing and other funding sources likely to cover the balance, the report said.
Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said the proposed investment could boost economic growth, create skilled jobs and expand opportunities for local suppliers.
He said Malaysia's data centre industry contributed RM14.1 billion to the economy this year, compared with RM900 million in 2021, highlighting the sector's rapid expansion.
However, he said the next challenge was ensuring that investment translated into broader economic benefits.
"Enforcing a 30 per cent local sourcing requirement would help generate a much higher domestic economic multiplier," he told Business Times.
Aimi said the investment could create skilled jobs in data centre management, engineering, cloud computing and AI, alongside indirect employment in construction and cybersecurity.
With unemployment at 2.9 per cent in August 2026, Aimi said Malaysia should focus on creating quality jobs that move workers into higher-value roles.
He said the government also wanted investors to go beyond providing facilities to house servers and support AI adoption, home-grown innovation and technology transfer.
He added that data centres in Johor had largely been "concrete shells", providing storage facilities rather than more advanced computing capabilities.
"Meaningful technology transfer would require giving local companies access to cloud infrastructure and training to use AI platforms, enabling them to develop higher-value digital capabilities," he said.
Aimi said local businesses could also benefit from procurement opportunities in cooling systems, electrical equipment, construction, engineering and professional services, provided they had the expertise and capacity to meet investors' needs.
On tax revenue, he said investment incentives could limit direct tax contributions from data centre operators, making taxes paid by local vendors and skilled workers, alongside utility payments, important sources of economic benefits.
He added that operators must pay market-rate, unsubsidised electricity tariffs and cover the cost of their full reserved electricity capacity, even if actual consumption is lower, to prevent subsidy leakage.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs), Datuk Mustapha Sakmud, said on Tuesday the US$50 billion investment in the AI sector in Sarawak is expected to serve as a new catalyst for economic growth in the Borneo region, particularly through the creation of high-skilled job opportunities and broader economic spillover effects.
"We highly welcome Sarawak's involvement in the AI ​​sector, as it will not only boost the state's economy and create career opportunities for locals, but the resulting benefits will also extend to Sabah.
"Wherever the Prime Minister goes on the international stage, he consistently highlights the potential of these two states," he said when met after appearing as a guest on the programme The Nation, produced by Bernama TV, at Wisma Bernama here today.
Meanwhile, Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said the proposed investment could strengthen Malaysia's digital economy, attract high-value activities and create skilled jobs in AI, cloud computing, cybersecurity and engineering.
However, he said the actual economic benefits would depend on how much of the proposed investment materialised and how effectively local businesses participated.
"Malaysia should prioritise technology transfer, local procurement, competitive wages and sustainable tax revenue rather than focusing solely on the investment figure.
"The ultimate measure of success is how much value remains within the domestic economy," he said.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said job quality and career progression should be key measures of the investment's success.
"I suppose the measure of success beyond GDP is how many high-quality, high-paying jobs are created for the locals," he said.
He said workers should also have opportunities to advance their careers and pursue further studies.
Afzanizam said Malaysia had a strong proposition for attracting technology investment, citing its peaceful environment, educated workforce, multicultural society and widespread English proficiency.
In July, S&P Global Ratings said Malaysia could nearly triple its data centre capacity by 2030, supported by its proximity to Singapore, strong connectivity and growing power and water capacity.
However, the rating agency said rising costs and tighter approval requirements posed execution challenges as the country shifted from rapid expansion towards more sustainable growth.
Companies that have been involved in AI data centres in Malaysia could benefit from the investment, which is touted as the largest single investment in the region.
Construction companies such as Gamuda Bhd, Sunway Construction Group Bhd, and MN Holdings Bhd are among the names that could bid for the project. In the power sector, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, YTL Power International Bhd, and Malakoff Corp Bhd are also in the line to benefit from such a massive project.
Renewable energy developers such as Solarvest Holdings Bhd, Samaiden Group Bhd, Pekat Group Bhd, Northern Solar Holdings Bhd and Cypark Resources Bhd could bid for Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (Cress) to support the investment.
In the water infrastructure, Salcon Engineering Bhd, Aliran Ihsan Resources Bhd, which is a member of MMC Group, and Ranhill Utilities Bhd could also benefit from the investment.
POWER AND WATER CAPACITY CRUCIAL FOR DATA CENTRE GROWTH
Aimi said Malaysia's infrastructure was not yet ready to support US$50 billion in data centre investments without further upgrades.
He said 57 data centres were operating with a combined power capacity of 6,237 megawatts (MW), while another 60 projects requiring 11,172MW were undergoing approval or construction.
"Data centres account for about 10 per cent of Malaysia's energy consumption, a figure expected to rise to one-third by 2035.
"BMI projects that data centres in Johor alone could consume 18 per cent of Peninsular Malaysia's electricity by 2031, up from six per cent in 2026," he said.
To manage demand, Aimi said the government required operators to commit to power purchase agreements of eight to 10 years before Tenaga Nasional Bhd expanded the grid.
Operators must also bear the cost of upgrading the transmission network, preventing households from shouldering expenses for electricity capacity that data centres may not fully use, he added.
Water availability is another concern, with a single 50MW data centre requiring about 788 million litres annually.
Aimi said the government was encouraging the use of reclaimed water and closed-loop cooling systems to reduce consumption.
For example, ZData's RM8 billion data centre in Gelang Patah, which has GreenRE Platinum certification, uses 100 per cent reclaimed water and plans to utilise 630,000 megawatt-hours of solar energy from 2028.
He also noted that a Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill was being drafted for submission to the Cabinet in 2027 to align industry growth with power and water capacity and promote circular economy practices.
Meanwhile, Idham said Malaysia had the capacity to support digital infrastructure expansion, but readiness depended on each project's location and requirements.
He said AI data centres require substantial electricity, reliable water supplies and resilient grid infrastructure.
"Rapid expansion without proper planning could strain utilities and undermine environmental sustainability.
"Investment approvals should therefore be aligned with confirmed infrastructure capacity, renewable energy development, water-efficient technologies and clear sustainability targets," he said.

Title: ECERDC beats target with RM10.3bil investments in 10 months [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The East Coast Economic Region Development Council (ECERDC) has exceeded its 2026 investment target, recording RM10.3 billion in realised investments in the first 10 months, or 104 per cent of its RM10 billion annual goal.
The investments across Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Johor's Mersing and Segamat districts are expected to create about 8,000 jobs, double the target of 4,000.
ECERDC also secured RM13.2 billion in committed investments, above its RM10 billion target.
These commitments are a pipeline of future investments that still depend on how projects are implemented.
ECERDC chief executive officer Syamsul Farizz Nadzeri said the jobs created reflect the economic opportunities opening up across the region.
He added that the council will keep working with investors, government partners and industry players to turn investments into real opportunities for local communities.
Terengganu led all states with RM4.8 billion in realised investments.
The biggest contributors were the RM2 billion expansion of Kemaman Port by Eastern Pacific Industrial Corporation Bhd and a RM1.9 billion floating solar farm by TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd.
Manufacturing added another RM600 million, including coated and plated steel, automotive components and other activities.
In Segamat, Johor, realised investments reached RM3.3 billion, driven by a hybrid solar plant developed by Lestra Hexa JV Sdn Bhd.
Pahang followed with RM1.7 billion, including a RM568 million integrated tourism centre by King's Park Development Sdn Bhd, a RM400 million sucralose manufacturing facility by Jinhe Nutrition (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd and a RM274 million durian farm by Upayapadu Resources Sdn Bhd.
Kelantan brought in RM600 million, meeting its state target.
Major projects there include a RM294.5 million large-scale solar project by Samaiden Legasi Timur Sdn Bhd, an RM88.5 million plantation project by DXN Biogreen Sdn Bhd and a RM48 million fruit and vegetable processing facility by Song Lin Fresh Fruit Hub Sdn Bhd.
Beyond the investment figures, ECERDC signed two memoranda of understanding (MoUs) to strengthen industrial and logistics development.
The first, with TGA Solutions Sdn Bhd, aims to promote investments in the Tanjung Agas Industrial Area in Pahang.
The second, with Infinity Landbridge Express Sdn Bhd, will explore investment and transport opportunities at Segamat Inland Port.
Infinity is investing RM30 million to reactivate the port as a rail-based logistics hub in southern Peninsular Malaysia.
It is expected to handle up to 6,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) of cargo a month, making freight movement more efficient and reducing reliance on road transport.
Several infrastructure projects have also made progress.
In Kelantan, the Palekbang-Kota Bharu Bridge and Tok Bali Industrial Park are 47 per cent and 54 per cent complete respectively, and both are on schedule.
In Pahang, the Kuantan Port Interchange was handed over on Sept 3, 2026, while main infrastructure works for Phase One, Package One of the Malaysia-China Kuantan Industrial Park 3 are complete.
According to ECERDC, the park could attract up to RM1.2 billion in investments.
In Terengganu, Phase One of the Kuala Terengganu City Centre Promenade received its Certificate of Completion and Compliance in June 2026, meaning it is ready for public use.
"Moving forward, our focus is to turn investment commitments into realised investments while advancing projects that strengthen the region's long-term competitiveness," Syamsul said.
"Through closer collaboration with investors and our development partners, we aim to accelerate implementation and expand sustainable economic opportunities across the East Coast."
