Title: UKM law faculty breaks into global top 100
Article:
BANGI: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's (UKM) Faculty of Law  entered the global top 100 for the first time, ranking 99th in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings by Subject 2026.
UKM vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Dr Sufian Jusoh announced the achievement at the opening of the Tuanku Chancellor International Conference on Law 2026 (TCC 2026) here yesterday.
The two-day conference was officiated by Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan and UKM chancellor Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir through a signing ceremony.
It brings together academics, policymakers, legal practitioners and researchers to examine the rule of law and good governance amid increasingly complex global challenges.
Present were Tuanku Muhriz's two sons, Tunku Besar of Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Panglima Besar of Negri Sembilan Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin, Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki, Philippine Ambassador to Malaysia Maria Angela Ponce and UKM Board of Directors chairman Datuk Johan Idris.
Sufian said the faculty's global ranking reflected years of dedication to teaching, research and scholarship, as well as the contributions of its staff and students.
"This milestone reflects years of dedication to teaching, research and scholarship, and the contributions of our staff and students."
The faculty's international achievements include winning the national round of the Philip C. Jessup International Law Moot Court Competition before finishing 11th in the global rounds in Washington.
UKM students also reached the top 16 at the 2026 Nuremberg Moot Court Competition, held at the Nuremberg Palace of Justice in Germany.
TCC 2026 is themed "Rule of Law and Good Governance in Post-Normal Times and Beyond".
It focuses on challenges facing legal systems amid technological developments, artificial intelligence, migration, trade, climate change, wars and security concerns.
Sufian said these developments underscored the need to strengthen legal principles and good governance across the region.
"Against this backdrop, TCC 2026 provides a platform to explore how legal principles can be strengthened in Asean, a region of growing importance, and how Malaysia can lead these conversations in the region."
He added that the two-day conference would also feature a round-table discussion  today titled "Strengthening the Rule of Law and Good Governance: Challenges and Future Directions".
The discussion will be chaired by Professor Tun Dr Tengku Maimun Tuan Mat, professor of practice at UKM's Faculty of Law and holder of the Tuanku Muhriz Royal Chair in Integrity and Good Governance.
Sufian said the rule of law and good governance remained central to UKM's TEKAD 57 strategic plan, which aims to contribute to a developed, principled and peaceful Malaysia by 2057, marking the country's centenary of independence.
In a separate development, UKM will establish an Asean Institute at the university, scheduled to be launched in April 2027 as a legacy of Malaysia's Asean chairmanship in 2025.
Sufian said UKM had contributed to regional cooperation through its involvement in developing key Asean policy frameworks and strategic documents, including the Asean Community Vision 2045, the Asean Economic Community Strategic Plan and the Asean Higher Education Declaration.
A UKM team had also worked with the Asean High-Level Task Force for the Asean Community Vision, assisting in the development of the regional vision.
The university also supported Malaysia's 2025 Asean chairmanship in completing 18 priority economic deliverables.
Several of these are being continued under the Philippines' chairmanship in 2026, Sufian added.
UKM is also part of the Asean University Network, contributing to regional strategic and vision documents and supporting the implementation of Asean initiatives.
Established in 2007, TCC provides a platform for dialogue on legal developments and governance challenges, bringing together expertise from academia, government and the legal profession.

Title: Leak website releases data on tens of thousands of DHS employees
Article:
WASHINGTON: The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it had released data on more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.
DHS did not respond to multiple messages seeking comment.
The disclosure — which the non-profit data transparency group said drew on information obtained by an entity calling itself "Department of Peace" — is the third major government data leak to make headlines in the past month.
In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees.
Last week, the Defence Department was hit with a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.
The DHS data includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and other DHS component agencies.
The data also included job titles and email groups, which, among other details, showed which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance, computer forensics and undercover work.
In a statement, Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder Emma Best said the hacktivist known as "maia arson crimew" had developed a search tool that would allow the public to browse the data.
Best said the tool would "replace anonymity with accountability" and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight.
The Department of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment. However, in a statement included with the data, it said DHS employees "have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs" and that it hoped the data "can be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction".
The Department of Peace claimed responsibility in March for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors.
Best's statement said the Department of Peace had harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS.
Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query: "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised."
Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the entire data trove but was able to match personal information about six DHS employees named in the leak with credit bureau records and breach data carried by the dark web intelligence platform District 4 Labs.
Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach.
In several cases, the data matched information available on DHS employees' LinkedIn profiles. In others, however, it revealed non-public details about internal DHS organisation charts or previously undisclosed programmes or operations.

Title: Anwar expresses deep sadness, extends condolences to Spain after deadly train collision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed deep grief over the tragic loss of lives in the train collision in Spain.
In a Facebook post, he said however Malaysia stood in solidarity with the people of Spain at this difficult time.
“Our thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones, and we wish the injured a swift recovery,” he said.
Anwar also paid tribute to the emergency personnel and others working tirelessly at the scene.
“On behalf of the Government and people of Malaysia, I extend our deepest condolences to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, the Government and people of Spain, and especially to the families of the victims,” prime minister said.
Yesterday, media reports said the death toll from Wednesday’s high-speed train collision in central Spain has more than doubled to at least 64 people, according to the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha, making it even deadlier than a devastating rail accident near Adamuz in January.
However, the Malaysian Embassy in Madrid has yet to receive confirmation of any Malaysians affected by the collision involving two high-speed passenger trains. — Bernama

Title: Anwar warns decline in reading and shallow thinking threaten civilisation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The decline of reading culture and the rise of shallow thinking in the digital age are pressing challenges that could threaten the future of civilisation, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In a Facebook post yesterday, the prime minister shared his thoughts after taking time to read the latest work by James Marriott, titled
The New Dark Ages: The End of Reading and the Dawn of a Post-Literate Society
.
He said the threat to civilisation does not stem from a loss of access to knowledge — of which there is now a glut — but from society’s waning love and patience for reading, reflecting, and thinking critically and deeply.
“We may be increasingly wealthy in information, yet impoverished in wisdom. The question, therefore, is not merely whether humanity still reads, but whether humanity still wants to think,” he said.
Reflecting on history, Anwar recalled society’s deep reverence for intellectual and literary traditions upon the death of great French writer Victor Hugo in 1885, which saw around two million people gather in Paris to pay their last respects.
He said a similar scene unfolded following the death of renowned Russian literary giant Fyodor Dostoevsky in 1881, when tens of thousands joined his funeral procession in Saint Petersburg, demonstrating how deeply society at the time valued literature, culture, intellectual traditions, and thought.
“Neither of them was a king nor a victorious warlord, but they were thinkers and scholars whose ideas resonated deeply in the hearts and minds of society,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Govt reaches 1.65 million people in Malaysia through Info on Wheels programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Information Department (Japen) has implemented the Info On Wheels (IOW) programme at 23,962 locations nationwide, reaching an audience of 1.65 million from January 1 to September 23, in an effort to expand the dissemination of information related to the Madani Government’s policies, assistance and initiatives.
The Communications Ministry said that 5,571 JIWA@Komuniti Madani: Sembang Santai programmes were also implemented during the same period, involving 616,961 members of the Madani Community to enhance public understanding of various government initiatives.
He said that the programme is among the government’s comprehensive, inclusive, and continuous communication strategies implemented through face-to-face approaches, narrative coordination, publication of communication materials and digital dissemination, taking into account the needs of different target groups.
“To ensure that the message conveyed is consistent and easily understood, 231 narratives and pointers related to policies, assistance, programmes, and achievements of the Madani Government have been prepared as a reference for field officers.
“The narrative encompasses four main frameworks, namely the economy for the people, leadership with integrity, national unity and consistent achievements, with an emphasis on explaining the benefits of policies to the people using easily understandable language,” the ministry stated in a written response on the Parliament portal today.
The ministry answered Suhaizan Kaiat’s (PH-Pulai) question regarding the government’s communication strategy in addressing the public’s confusion about government policies and benefits, which makes them easily influenced by false information and propaganda.
In expanding digital reach, the ministry reported that 9,294 posts were uploaded on Japen’s official social media, including 1,298 creative content pieces that recorded 16.51 million views as of September 22.
It said the effort was supported through the publication of 50 brochures, 35 bulletins and four booklets, in addition to organising 68 exhibitions that attracted 162,900 visitors and the use of 4,000 screens through strategic partners.
It also said that the government will continue to strengthen integrated communication through various channels to ensure that the people receive accurate, clear, and easily understandable information, thereby enabling them to make fact-based assessments and not be easily swayed by misleading narratives.
Meanwhile, in response to Datuk Siti Aminah Aching’s (BN-Beaufort) question regarding the level of high-speed internet coverage and the issue of weak or no internet access in that parliamentary area, the Ministry of Communications said that 37 areas were identified as experiencing problems with that facility from January 1 to September 1.
Following that, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) issued 104 Notices of Non-Compliance to service providers between March 11 and August 5 to obtain improvement plans at the affected locations.
“A total of 51 instances of non-compliance have been resolved through the optimisation of the existing network, while another 33 will be addressed via improvements to network coverage and capacity. The remaining 20 require further action through a Commission Directive,” the ministry stated.
The ministry also said that internet and communication coverage in the populated areas of the Beaufort parliamentary constituency has reached 99.57 per cent as of Sept 1 through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela), with 29 communication towers completed, 113 transmitter stations upgraded, and 7,526 premises equipped with fibre optic access.
For the 5G network, Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) provides coverage to 20 per cent of populated areas through one transmitter site, while U Mobile Sdn Bhd achieves 42.80 per cent coverage through five upgraded transmitter sites as of the same date. — Bernama

Title: Orange economy state-level meeting expected in November, Fahmi says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — A meeting involving state executive councillors (Exco members) to discuss developments in the orange economy is expected to be held in the third week of November or by the end of the month, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the proposed working committee would involve state Exco members and ministers to discuss the progress of the orange economy in their respective states.
Fahmi said he had recently presented a note on the proposed establishment of the committee at the Meeting of Mentris Besar and Chief Ministers.
He said the discussions would focus on feedback and proposals from state governments, including identifying potential film locations, craft products, cultural groups and animation teams that could be promoted and supported.
“This is important because we need to obtain feedback, views, findings and proposals from Exco members and state ministers on the creative economy,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the Lembah Pantai Parliamentary Deepavali Aid Presentation Ceremony at IWK Eco Park@Pantai Dalam here last night, organised by the Lembah Pantai Member of Parliament’s Office in collaboration with Minnal FM.
Also present were Communications Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Telecommunications Infrastructure) Mano Verabathran and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Editor-in-Chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj.
Fahmi said the government needed time to obtain feedback from state governments before the Orange Economy Council met again.
“We need a little more time at that level. We expect the Orange Economy Council to meet again in the first quarter of next year,” he said.
The Orange Economy Council (MEJ) was established a few months ago and is chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, with membership comprising several ministries.
Earlier, Fahmi presented RM150 vouchers to about 600 families in the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency in conjunction with Deepavali to help ease their cost of living and festive preparations.
He said the vouchers could be redeemed at selected outlets, including Checkers Hypermarket, Mydin Mart Pantai Dalam, TMC Bangsar and Econsave Scott Garden in Jalan Klang Lama, from October 23 to November 18, 2026.
Fahmi said the government had also introduced various initiatives to assist the Indian community, including an allocation of RM150 million through the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (MITRA), as well as RM150 million each through Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM) and the National Entrepreneurial Group Economic Fund (Tekun).
He said cooperation with relevant agencies and Minnal FM would be undertaken to improve the Indian community’s understanding of and access to the various government assistance programmes available.
In Lembah Pantai, Fahmi said efforts were also being made to improve facilities at Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) Bangsar and SJKT Saraswathy, both categorised as under-enrolled schools. These included purchasing new laptops for their computer laboratories and upgrading infrastructure.
“This is important to me. I want these two Tamil national-type schools to remain in Lembah Pantai. We will ensure that they can continue operating,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Umno confirms pact with PAS, Perikatan for Melaka polls, to launch joint manifesto
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Umno has confirmed its political cooperation with PAS and Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the 16th Melaka state election, which will include a joint election manifesto between Barisan Nasional (BN) and PN.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision was made at the party’s supreme council meeting yesterday.
He said Umno had directed all its election machinery and supporters to give their full backing to PN candidates contesting in the state election.
“(The meeting) unanimously agreed to formalise the political cooperation and understanding with our strategic partner PAS and our friends from Perikatan Nasional to face the 16th Melaka state election.
“We also agreed for BN and PN to launch a joint election manifesto to offer the best service to the people and to continue the excellence in the state’s administration and development that has been achieved so far,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Asyraf Wajdi also called on party leaders and machinery to campaign courteously and ethically throughout the election period.
He said all parties should avoid slander, insults and personal attacks against rival parties to ensure a mature and harmonious campaign.
Separately, he urged the government, particularly the Finance Ministry, to withdraw its directive cancelling projects that involve the people’s interests, especially in Sabah and Sarawak.
He said rural development projects, including road construction and rural water and electricity supply, must continue for the wellbeing and development of local communities.

Title: Sabah, Sarawak rural road funding has not been cancelled, says minister
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 29 — Allegations regarding the cancellation or reduction of allocations for the rural road projects (JALB) in Sabah and Sarawak by the Madani Government need to be examined based on accurate facts and information, said the Sabah PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.
In this regard, he suggested that any party raising the matter should provide detailed information, including an official list of projects, allocation values and their implementation status.
Mustapha, who is also the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs), said that the directive to postpone the issuance of new Letters of Acceptance (SST) dated September 10 was an internal financial control measure to prevent the increase of contract commitments exceeding the annual ceiling and not the cancellation of approved development projects.
“The fact is, the original allocation for JALB at the national level continues to increase from RM2.11 billion for the year 2026 to RM2.27 billion for the year 2027, compared to the previous era which never reached RM1 billion before Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration initiated an allocation of RM1.09 billion in 2023.
“In fact, the Ministry of Finance has approved an additional expenditure of RM500 million in 2026 to help address the backlog of payments to JALB contractors to ensure the commitments of existing projects can be fulfilled,” he said.
He said this after chairing a special coordination meeting of the Kota Kinabalu Disaster Committee at Kota Kinabalu City Hall here today.
Mustapha said the federal government’s continued commitment to the development of the Borneo region is reflected in Budget 2027, which allocates RM18.7 billion to Sabah compared to RM17.6 billion previously, while the allocation for Sarawak is increased from RM15.1 billion to RM16.2 billion.
“Meanwhile, an amount of RM3.3 billion has also been allocated specifically for the implementation of road projects in Sabah and Sarawak, covering the continuation of the development of strategic road networks,” he also said.
He emphasised that the development of basic facilities in Sabah and Sarawak remains a long-term investment priority of the Madani Government to strengthen connectivity and bridge the gap between regions. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan sticks to 21-seat target for Melaka polls for now, Fahmi says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is maintaining its decision to contest 21 seats in the Melaka state election for now, with any changes subject to a final decision by the coalition’s top leadership.
PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the coalition will concentrate on the seats that have already been announced.
“We have announced 21 seats. If there are any changes, we leave it to the leadership to announce,” he told reporters at a Deepavali contribution event for the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency at IWK Eco Park @ Pantai Dalam last night.
Fahmi said PH will evaluate its participation in the state polls based on its own capacity and capabilities, taking into account strategic and tactical considerations.
“We know several other parties will announce their candidates tomorrow. That is their prerogative, but our considerations are grounded in Pakatan Harapan’s own capabilities,” he said.
Media reports previously indicated that PH was poised to contest three additional seats in the election, with PKR allocated one more seat and Amanah two.
If finalised, the move would see PH contest 24 of the 28 state seats in Melaka. — Bernama

Title: Melaka BN resolves seat dispute with MCA ahead of state polls, Ab Rauf says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The seat allocation issue within Barisan Nasional (BN) involving component party MCA for the upcoming Melaka state election has been resolved, says Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He said negotiations had reached an agreement, adding that MCA’s participation as the party representing the Chinese community within BN would be refined and enhanced.
“MCA is okay, settled. Done deal. MCA accepts it as it is, and MCA’s participation representing the Chinese community will certainly be refined and enhanced, Insya-Allah,” he told reporters after attending an UMNO Supreme Council meeting at Menara Dato’ Onn here last night.
Commenting on matters discussed during the meeting, Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said party machinery had been directed to focus election work on the 21 state seats BN is contesting.
He said State Executive Council members appointed as mentors for specific constituencies have also been tasked with assisting the Melaka BN machinery to secure victory across all contested seats.
“Every vote is crucial for us to defend the 21 seats we are contesting,” he said.
Ab Rauf confirmed that an understanding with BN component parties on election ground operations had been finalised.
Yesterday, Ab Rauf and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong broke the impasse over seat allocations for the Melaka state election scheduled for next month.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka BN election director, described the outcome of the discussions as positive.
MCA had previously stated it would not recognise any party candidates announced by BN for the Melaka polls without the endorsement of its top leadership.
Last Saturday, BN announced its candidates for 21 state seats, including two from MCA, namely Machap Jaya incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem and Kelebang incumbent Datuk Lim Ban Hong.
Nomination day for the Melaka state election is scheduled for this Saturday, while early voting and polling day have been set for November 10 and 14, respectively. — Bernama

Title: Police seize 376kg of pangolin scales worth RM376,200 in Negeri Sembilan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Police detained three local men and seized 376.2kg of pangolin scales worth an estimated RM376,200 in an integrated operation at a premises in Negeri Sembilan on Tuesday.
The operation, which began at 12.30pm, was carried out by the Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence Division (WCB/PSK) of Bukit Aman’s Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA), in collaboration with the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan), under Operasi Bersepadu Khazanah (OBK).
In a statement yesterday, Bukit Aman WCB/PSK JKDNKA Commander SAC Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said police found 15 boxes of pangolin scales during a search of the premises, suspected to be linked to the storage and distribution of products derived from protected wildlife.
“Other items seized during the operation included nine mobile phones of various brands, a weighing scale and a padlock.
“The total value of the seizure, including other items, is estimated at RM401,700,” he said, adding that police took all suspects and seized items to the Nilai District Police Headquarters before handing them over to Perhilitan investigators for further action.
Mohd Zaki said the case was being investigated under Section 68 of the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716), relating to offences involving wildlife, its parts or derivatives.
“This large-scale seizure underscores the importance of continued intelligence and enforcement operations to combat networks involved in storing, collecting and distributing products derived from wildlife,” he said.
Mohd Zaki said the division had carried out 288 raids nationwide between Jan 1 and today, involving various offences, including wildlife smuggling, untaxed goods, leakage of controlled and subsidised goods, and e-waste-related activities that resulted in 471 arrests, with the total value of seizures estimated at RM350.35 million.
He said 66 cases were recorded this year, involving 74 arrests and seizures worth an estimated RM99.70 million under the OBK. — Bernama

Title: MACC probe into KWAP’s eFishery investment ongoing, Finance Ministry says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is still investigating Retirement Fund Incorporated’s (KWAP) investment in Indonesian aquaculture technology company eFishery, the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said yesterday.
The ongoing investigation has not uncovered any evidence of criminal wrongdoing involving corruption or misappropriation, as reported by the media on August 13, 2026, the ministry said.
KWAP has also cooperated with relevant authorities and the investor consortium in taking appropriate action against those responsible, MoF added.
“At the same time, efforts are continuing through appropriate channels to maximise the recovery of the investment value,” it said in a written reply on the Parliament website yesterday.
MoF was responding to a question from Tuan Kalam Salan (PN-Sabak Bernam), who wanted to know KWAP’s investment of about RM200 million in eFishery.
Tuan Kalam also requested clarification on the investment approval, the parties responsible for the due diligence failure, total losses, and whether KWAP will take action against the negligent, MoF said.
The eFishery investment underwent established assessment and governance processes, including verification by a qualified international auditor based on the information available at the time, MoF said.
The company was, however, subsequently found to have engaged in financial manipulation and misrepresentation of facts in its financial reports.
“The assessment process before investment approval also included internal evaluations, independent due diligence, and reviews of financial, legal and operational aspects. Several major global institutional investors were also affected by the misconduct,” the ministry said.
The actual investment amounted to RM163.4 million, a 2.51 per cent equity stake.
KWAP is a minority shareholder in eFishery. Other investors, including major global institutional investors, hold most of the company’s shares, it added. — Bernama

Title: Rice smuggling bid foiled in Gua Musang: 25 tonnes of Thai rice seized, driver held over dubious invoices
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 29 — The General Operations Force (GOF) has seized a lorry carrying 25 metric tonnes of Super Import white rice suspected to have been smuggled in from Thailand, during an operation in Paloh here last night.
Sinar Harian
reported that the rice and the lorry seized in the 11pm operation, codenamed Op Taring Wawasan, were worth an estimated RM550,000 in total.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said personnel on patrol spotted a suspicious lorry near Kampung Pangkal Senor, along the Kota Bharu-Gua Musang highway.
He said the lorry was stopped for inspection by the roadside of Jalan Bentong-Kota Bharu, in front of a building.
“The inspection found that the lorry was carrying Super Import white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand.
“The driver produced two copies of invoices to explain the source and destination of the rice, but there were doubts over the delivery location stated in the documents,” he told reporters this morning.
Ahmad Radzi said this led to the arrest of the 38-year-old driver to assist in investigations.
He said the lorry, the entire load of rice and the two invoices were seized and handed over to the Kelantan office of the National Paddy and Rice Regulatory (KPB) for further action.
“Initial checks found that the delivery location stated in the invoices was inaccurate, raising suspicion that the documents were used to mislead the authorities about the true source and purpose of the shipment.
“However, the authenticity of the documents is still under investigation,” he was quoted as saying.
According to the Malay daily, Ahmad Radzi said investigations would be widened to identify the source of supply, those who prepared and used the invoices, the transporter, the recipient and the distribution network for the suspected smuggled rice.
The case is being investigated under Section 20 of the Control of Padi and Rice Act 1994.

Title: Foreigner arrested over alleged assault on auxiliary policeman at Genting casino
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 29 — A foreign national has been arrested for allegedly injuring an auxiliary police officer and damaging casino equipment at Sky Casino in Genting Highlands, Bentong, on Tuesday.
Acting Bentong district police chief DSP Azmi Mahmod said preliminary investigations revealed that the 34-year-old man, believed to have been drunk, had allegedly behaved aggressively towards members of the public before entering the casino.
He said the suspect then allegedly damaged the screens of three gambling machines by repeatedly banging his head against them, as well as two chairs, resulting in estimated losses of RM85,000.
“The suspect sustained a forehead injury that required six stitches,” Azmi said in a statement today.
He said the man also allegedly punched a 32-year-old auxiliary police officer in the mouth, breaking two of his teeth.
Azmi said the officer had since received treatment at Bentong Hospital.
Initial checks revealed that the suspect had no previous criminal record and had tested negative for drugs, he said.
The case is being investigated under Sections 323 and 427 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and committing mischief resulting in property damage, respectively. — Bernama

Title: Fallen trees hit six vehicles in Selangor, no casualties reported
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Five fallen tree incidents were reported at several locations in Selangor from yesterday afternoon to last night, affecting six vehicles that were struck by trees or branches, with no casualties reported.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the first incident occurred at Jalan MR 1/6, Rawang, at 4.40pm, when a tree belonging to the Selayang Municipal Council fell onto three vehicles.
“The vehicles involved were a Hyundai Santa Fe, Proton Iriz and Perodua Axia. A team from the Batu Arang Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 4.54 pm, with four personnel and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) deployed,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said the second incident occurred at 5.05pm at the Education Quarters in Persiaran Indera Wawasan, Pusat Bandar Puchong, when a tree fell onto a Toyota Vios.
A team from the Puchong Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 5.14pm. The operation was brought under control at 5.16 pm and concluded a minute later, with seven personnel involved, he said.
Meanwhile, a fallen tree incident was reported by a member of the public on the Threads platform at 5.10pm along the Kerinchi Link Expressway, from Bangsar towards Bukit Damansara.
A post by Threads user @rmasyraf showed a fallen tree on the road and rescue personnel at the scene.
However, further details of the incident, including the number of vehicles affected, could not be obtained as the Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department had not received any report.
Ashrul Riezal said two more incidents were reported in the evening. At 6.44pm, a tree branch fell onto a Honda CR-V at Jalan DM 3/7, Taman Desa Rawang, while at 6.49pm, a tree fell onto a Proton Saga at Akasia Apartment, Jalan Wawasan 2/3, Puchong.
“For the incident in Taman Desa Rawang, a team from the Rawang Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 6.55pm, with eight personnel, an FRT and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle deployed.
“For the incident at Akasia Apartment, a team from the Puchong Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 6.55pm, with seven personnel and an FRT deployed. Both reports stated that there were no casualties, but the times when the operations were brought under control and concluded were not specified,” he said.
Overall, the four incidents reported to the fire and rescue department involved six vehicles, while the fifth incident along the Kerinchi Link Expressway was known through a public post on Threads. The total number of vehicles affected in all five incidents could not be confirmed. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia records 3,581 child abuse cases in first half of 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Social Welfare Department (JKM) recorded a total of 3,581 cases of physical, sexual and emotional abuse involving children in the first six months of this year.
The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) said 1,522 cases were recorded in the first quarter (January to March), with the number rising to 2,059 in the second quarter (April to June).
The ministry disclosed the figures in a written reply published on the Parliament website today in response to a question from Sabri Azit (PN-Jerai) on child abuse and neglect cases recorded in the first and second quarters of 2026, as well as the number of cases brought to court.
KPWKM also highlighted an upward trend in cases involving child neglect and abandonment during the same period.
“JKM recorded 987 cases of abandonment, including child neglect, in the first quarter of 2026.  The number rose to 1,292 in the second quarter, bringing the total to 2,279 cases for the first half of the year,” the ministry said.
KPWKM also said that as of June 2026, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) had opened 867 investigation papers into child abuse cases, with 267 cases brought to court.
The ministry stressed that it remained committed to safeguarding children’s welfare and safety through JKM, in accordance with the provisions of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611).
It said JKM was responsible for rescuing victims, arranging safe accommodation and providing rehabilitation support.
The department had also stepped up efforts under the Child Protection Advocacy Programme: KASIH Kanak-Kanak since 2023, KPWKM said.
“A total of 220 KASIH Kanak-Kanak programmes were conducted at 220 schools between January and September 2026, involving 57,012 participants comprising children, parents and teachers.
“Since 2023, the programme has been implemented at 1,244 schools and 74 children’s activity centres, involving more than 270,000 participants,” the ministry said.
KPWKM urged the public to report cases of child neglect or abuse through the 24-hour Talian Kasih hotline at 15999 or via WhatsApp at 019-2615999 to facilitate prompt intervention and rescue efforts. — Bernama

Title: Learn from Indonesia-Singapore gas row, build up own energy resources, maritime expert tells govt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Indonesia’s move to cut natural gas exports to Singapore should be a reminder for Malaysia to develop and maximise its own natural resources to strengthen energy security, according to a maritime industry player.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said countries must ensure that their natural resources and energy infrastructure support domestic needs and long-term economic interests.
“Indonesia is effectively saying: do not take us for a ride. Before questioning what Indonesia is doing, look at your own operators and examine what they have received from Indonesia over the years,” he said in a statement this morning.
Indonesia began reducing natural gas exports to Singapore on Oct 24. It is redirecting some supplies from Natuna and Sumatra to meet its own energy needs.
Jakarta has maintained that the reduction remains within the minimum volumes stipulated in its supply contracts.
Jeyenderan said the development showed how energy security could become intertwined with bilateral relations, particularly when countries depended on cross-border supplies of strategic commodities.
He said Malaysia should take note of regional developments by placing greater emphasis on developing its own resources, strengthening domestic energy capabilities and ensuring its infrastructure supported long-term national interests.
“Malaysia should also maximise the economic value of its strategic location along major international shipping routes, particularly through the development of its bunkering industry,” he said.
He said bunkering, the supply of fuel to ships, was an opportunity for Malaysia to earn revenue from its petroleum resources, port infrastructure and maritime services, while strengthening its position as a regional shipping and energy hub.
Greater attention to the industry could help Malaysia capture more of the economic benefits from vessels passing through the region, including through fuel supply, storage and related maritime services, he added.
Jeyenderan also pointed to Singapore’s efforts to diversify its energy sources, including through liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports and strategic relationships with major global suppliers.
He cited the recent announcement by Singapore and Saudi Arabia that Saudi crude oil would be stored at the Jurong Rock Caverns from the second half of 2027 to strengthen supply security.
“Why is Aramco going to Singapore? It is because Singapore understands that energy security is not simply about buying oil or gas today. It is about securing supply, storage, logistics and strategic relationships for the future,” he said.
He said Malaysia should pay close attention because Saudi Aramco was also an important strategic partner for the country through its downstream investments with Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) in Pengerang, Johor.
Jeyenderan said Malaysia should continue strengthening its relationships with major energy-producing countries and companies, while ensuring its own natural resources were developed effectively to support domestic needs and economic growth.
He said international partnerships remained important, but countries also needed to ensure their domestic resources, infrastructure and long-term energy strategies were aligned with national interests.
“What is happening between Indonesia and Singapore is a reminder for everyone in the region.
“Energy security is about relationships, infrastructure and knowing who you can rely on when supply becomes tight. Malaysia must protect those relationships before a crisis happens,” he said.

Title: Newborn buried alive in Kapit in critical condition
Article:
KAPIT, Oct 29 —  A newborn baby boy was found buried alive near a rented house on Jalan Airport here on Tuesday.
Kapit district police chief DSP Rohana Nanu said the baby was found by police officers after hearing its cries while conducting a search in the area.
She said the incident was reported to have occurred around 2.30pm yesterday.
“The baby boy was found by the police during a search at the scene after hearing the cries of the baby. The newborn was found buried,” she said when contacted today.
Rohana said the baby was in critical condition and would be sent to Sibu Hospital for further treatment.
She added that a female suspect has been identified, but her statement has not yet been recorded as she is still receiving treatment at the hospital.
According to her, the case is being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: AI literacy, Brics role and AI Bill on the agenda
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Ministry of Education’s plans to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) literacy into the school curriculum, Malaysia’s participation as a Brics partner country, and the drafting of an AI Governance Bill are among the key topics set to be addressed in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper available on the Parliament website, during the Ministers’ Question Time, Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (PN-Merbok) will ask the Minister of Education to outline the Ministry’s plans to incorporate AI literacy into the school curriculum through the AI Literacy Guide.
Following this, the proceedings will continue with a question-and-answer session, during which Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) will ask the Minister of Foreign Affairs to explain the objectives behind Malaysia’s participation as a BRICS partner country, as well as the added value this offers compared to existing bilateral cooperation.
Additionally, Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) will pose a question to the Minister of Digital regarding the status of the drafting of the AI Governance Bill, the expected timeline for its tabling in the Dewan Rakyat, and the existing legal protections available to citizens who fall victim to fraud.
Datuk Seri Doris Sophia anak Brodi (GPS-Sri Aman) will ask the Minister of Foreign Affairs to provide the number of Malaysians detained or charged for drug-related offences abroad over the last five years, as well as to comment on the effectiveness of airport scanning technology in detecting drugs and the current state of security.
During the same session, Datuk Seri Sh Mohmed Puzi Sh Ali (BN-Pekan) will ask the Minister of Agriculture and Food Security to provide statistics on the economic returns generated by the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Show (MAHA), and to what extent the event has benefited small-scale operators.
The winding-up session for the debate on the Supply Bill 2027, scheduled for tomorrow, will involve several ministries including the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities, the Ministry of Communications, the Ministry of Human Resources, the Ministry of Economy, the Ministry of Youth and Sports, and the Ministry of Finance before the Dewan Rakyat proceeds to a vote to pass the Bill. — Bernama

Title: Inside KL’s SMART Tunnel: The hidden work behind its flood-fighting operation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — On a daily basis, motorists driving through the motorway section of Kuala Lumpur’s SMART Tunnel may pass through without giving much thought to the two gates that remain shut beyond the familiar stretch of road.
Yet behind those gates lies another side of the tunnel — never seen by motorists.
During a visit to the facility, a current of air from the flood tunnel felt surprisingly cool against the skin, almost like a breeze offering relief from the heat outside.
This was coming from the 9.7km-long infrastructure beneath the city that is part of a flood-mitigation system designed to divert excess water from the confluence of Sungai Klang and Sungai Ampang at Kampung Berembang towards a holding pond in Taman Desa.
Only about 3km of the tunnel doubles as a motorway.
When heavy rain threatens to overwhelm the river system, that section can be closed to traffic so the tunnel can fulfil its other purpose: carrying floodwater away from vulnerable parts of Kuala Lumpur.
Constructing the tunnel required specialised underground engineering —a 13.2-metre-diameter Slurry Mix-Shield tunnel-boring machine (TBM) to excavate the passage beneath the city.
The machine was among the largest of its kind in the region at the time, helping create the stormwater tunnel that now serves two very different purposes, depending on the weather.
What happens behind the gates when the weather turns?
Two control centres, one flood threat
The first signs of a possible flood operation emerge well before water enters the motorway section.
The Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) monitors river conditions and water levels, assessing the threat posed by rising water and managing the diversion of excess flows.
Meanwhile, Amanat Lebuhraya Rakyat Berhad’s (ALR) SMART Traffic Control Centre oversees traffic operations, including traffic diversions and motorway closures.
ALR, is the holding company of the SMART Tunnel concessionaire.
When the threat of flooding requires the motorway to be closed, traffic must first be cleared and the road secured before the tunnel can be used for flood mitigation.
These warnings — through various channels, today via social media platforms — begin when Mode 3 is activated, as the motorway is closed and motorists are advised to avoid the SMART Tunnel and use alternative routes.
Mode 3 is a precautionary measure that places the tunnel on standby for possible flooding.
Although the motorway is closed, the traffic compartment is not necessarily flooded at this stage.
Only if heavy rain persists, Mode 4 is activated and the motorway compartment is used to trap floodwater.
Amanat Lebuhraya Rakyat Bhd group chief executive officer Muhammad Nizam Alias speaks during a visit and media briefing at the SMART Tunnel in Kuala Lumpur on October 21, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif.
What happens behind the gates?
Under normal conditions, the motorway remains open and the gates stay shut.
Most motorists have little reason to think about what lies beyond them.
The tunnel is designed to operate in four modes, depending on rainfall and flood conditions.
Under Mode 1, the motorway operates normally, with no floodwater diverted through the tunnel.
In Mode 2, excess water is channelled through the lower section while the road remains open to traffic.
When a more serious storm threatens, the system moves to Mode 3, then subsequently, Mode 4 is activated if the rain arrives at a threatening stage.
For the first time in nearly 20 years, the gates were opened for viewing to the press, offering a glimpse of the tunnel’s interior.
Once diverted, excess water is channelled towards Taman Desa Pond, where it is temporarily stored before being released into Sungai Kerayong through a separate, approximately 500m-long twin box culvert.
The gates are only one part of a system that also relies on river monitoring, traffic control, water diversion and storage.
Since the tunnel began operating in 2007, Mode 4 has been activated 11 times, turning the motorway into a flood channel when heavy rain threatens Kuala Lumpur.
When the rain stops, work continues
After a Mode 4 operation, floodwater must be pumped out and debris removed before the tunnel can be restored for traffic.
About 30m underground, seven floors below ground level, there is the Pump Room that houses five large pumps.
These large pumps are responsible for draining water that’s been trapped in the tunnel.
Floodwater can leave behind mud, sediment, driftwood and other debris, while the force of the water may also damage lights, signboards and other tunnel fixtures.
Crews must check for gas and other potential hazards before proceeding with cleaning.
The recovery process is estimated to take an average of about two days, with a reopening target of up to four days after closure.
RM500,000 in average repair costs
The physical damage caused by floodwater also carries a substantial cost and could be estimated at RM500,00 each time Mode 4 was activated.
There is also a financial trade-off when the motorway closes. During Modes 3 and 4, vehicles cannot use the motorway section, meaning toll collection through that section stops while the road is unavailable to traffic.
A general view of the SMART Tunnel during a visit and media briefing in Kuala Lumpur on October 21, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif.
Awaiting the next storm
For motorists, the SMART Tunnel may be little more than a few kilometres of road beneath Kuala Lumpur. Its other function is largely invisible during ordinary journeys.
Behind the closed gates is a system that must be monitored and prepared before floodwater can be diverted, then drained, cleaned and repaired before traffic can return.
Ventilation, pumping and maintenance all play a part in keeping the infrastructure ready for the moment it must change purpose.
The cool breeze ends once the visit was over, it was lights-off and the tunnel was left in pitch darkness, awaiting the next time it would be called into service.

Title: A road when it’s dry, a river when it pours: How KL’s SMART Tunnel switches from highway to flood channel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — To most motorists, the SMART Tunnel is a way to bypass traffic congestion on the southern approach to Kuala Lumpur’s city centre. Its primary purpose, however, goes beyond moving vehicles.
The 9.7km Stormwater Management and Road Tunnel combines a 3km double-deck motorway with a flood-control system designed to divert excess water away from the city centre during heavy rain.
It channels water from the Klang-Ampang catchment to reduce downstream flood risks, including around the confluence of the Klang and Gombak rivers near Masjid Jamek.
According to Amanat Lebuhraya Rakyat (ALR), the holding company of the SMART Tunnel concessionaire and three other highway concessionaires, the system has a combined water-storage capacity of three million cubic metres and has recorded 685 flood-mode incidents.
Project documentation puts the overall cost at approximately RM1.93 billion.
Why was the SMART Tunnel built?
Kuala Lumpur has a long history of flooding, with major events recorded in 1926 and 1971.
In April 2001, floods inundated Jalan Ipoh, Jalan Gombak and Jalan Munshi Abdullah.
Further incidents in June 2002 and June 2003 affected areas around the Klang River, Jalan Gombak and Dataran Merdeka.
The 9.7km-long floodwater tunnel that channels floodwater to the Taman Desa holding pond. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
The SMART Tunnel idea emerged in 2001, when the government sought private-sector proposals to address recurring floods while easing congestion on the southern approach to the city centre.
How was the dual-purpose model developed?
Gamuda Berhad, working with engineering consultants Sepakat Setia Perunding Sdn Bhd and Mott MacDonald, developed a flood-diversion tunnel proposal before partnering MMC Corporation Berhad in 2002 to incorporate a motorway.
The project involved both the government and private sector, with the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and Malaysian Highway Authority among the agencies involved.
The government commissioned the stormwater management component to divert floodwater from the Klang-Ampang catchment through the tunnel and into downstream storage.
Meanwhile, the motorway was developed under a privatisation arrangement based on a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) model.
The private-sector joint venture formed Syarikat Mengurus Air Banjir dan Terowong Sdn Bhd to implement the project and operate the motorway concession.
Construction began in 2003, and the tunnel opened to traffic in 2007.
How does the tunnel work?
The pump room located 30 metres below ground level. — Picture by Firdaus Latif.
The SMART Tunnel forms part of an integrated system that diverts excess water from the Klang and Ampang rivers towards downstream storage facilities.
According to ALR, the system has a combined capacity of three million cubic metres, equivalent to about 1,200 Olympic-sized swimming pools. This comprises:
Kampung Berembang holding pond: 600,000 cubic metres
SMART Tunnel: one million cubic metres
Taman Desa holding pond: 1.4 million cubic metres
During heavy rain, excess water is diverted into the system near Kampung Berembang and channelled towards Taman Desa for temporary storage before being released into Sungai Kerayong.
Two control centres oversee different aspects of the operation:
SMART Control Centre: Under DID, it monitors rainfall and river flows, issues flood warnings and directs water into the system.
Motorway Control Centre: Operated by ALR, it manages traffic diversion and clearing, as well as cleaning and restoring the road before reopening.
Safety features include 220 CCTV cameras monitored around the clock, variable-message traffic signs, 42 emergency telephones, 16 radio units, watertight doors and 10 emergency exits and escape routes.
There are four tunnel modes
Mode 1: Normal operation
During ordinary weather, traffic uses the motorway as usual, with no floodwater diverted through the tunnel.
Mode 2: Heavy rain
When water levels rise, excess water is diverted through the lower channel beneath the motorway, allowing traffic to continue. ALR’s operating matrix identifies a flow range of 70 to 150 cubic metres per second for this mode.
Mode 3: Motorway closure
When the flood model forecasts a flow rate of 150 cubic metres per second or more, the motorway is closed and cleared of vehicles in preparation for possible floodwater diversion.
The motorway compartments may not need to be flooded if conditions change.
Mode 4: Prolonged severe storm
If the storm persists, the motorway compartments are used to carry floodwater after all vehicles have been evacuated.
The motorway remains closed until the water has been drained and the road cleaned and inspected.
The distinction is important: a motorway closure does not necessarily mean the tunnel will be flooded.
Mode 3 prepares it for possible use as a floodwater channel, while Mode 4 involves diverting water through the motorway tunnel.
Closure of the SMART tunnel also meant that no tolls are collected throughout the flooding of the tunnel and recovery stages.
The numbers are an illustration only, not verified current losses.
Actual foregone revenue would depend on current toll revenue, traffic patterns, timing of closure, and whether traffic would otherwise have paid the toll.
What happens after the tunnel floods?
The tunnel cannot immediately reopen once a floodwater diversion operation ends. According to ALR, recovery involves six stages:
Stage1: Notification — DID issues a notification and monitors river flows and water levels.
Stage 2: Pumping — Floodwater is pumped out and the main flow checked.
Stage 3: Safety inspection — The tunnel is checked for gas and other potential hazards.
Stage 4: Cleaning — Machinery removes debris and sediment, with operations running around the clock.
Stage 5: System restoration — The tunnel’s systems are restored and checked.
Stage 6: Final inspection — Safety checks are completed before the motorway reopens.
This is a four-day reopening target, with an average recovery period of two days. The actual duration depends on the work needed to restore safe operating conditions.
Major maintenance may also be required after Mode 4, including replacing tunnel fixtures or repairing structural damage caused by floodwater.
How much flood damage has the tunnel prevented?
ALR reported 685 flood-mode incidents and estimated that the system had avoided RM4.94 billion in potential flood damage.
The incidents comprised 556 Mode 2 operations, 118 Mode 3 operations and 11 Mode 4 operations.
The estimates also cover areas and populations ALR said were protected during these operations. They represent potential damage avoided, rather than a direct accounting of losses that would certainly have occurred without the tunnel.
While the SMART Tunnel’s primary purpose remains flood mitigation, its motorway component also operates under a toll concession. Its financing and management arrangements have since changed as the government sought to reduce compensation payments, avoid toll increases and bring forward the return of the concessions to the government.
Why was the concession restructured?
The restructuring covered four Klang Valley highway concessions: SMART, KESAS, LDP and SPRINT.
Under the original agreements, the government faced compensation payments when tolls were kept below the rates concessionaires were contractually entitled to charge.
For SMART, ALR previously cited a contractual toll of RM5 for a Class 1 vehicle, compared with the prevailing rate of RM3 at the time. The contractual rate was scheduled to rise further.
The restructuring aimed to address three issues:
Reduce government compensation: The government had been paying concessionaires the difference between the tolls motorists paid and the rates stipulated in their agreements.
Avoid toll hikes: Without restructuring, the government would have had to continue paying compensation or allow toll rates to rise.
Shorten the concessions: Revenue would go towards debt repayment instead of shareholder dividends, allowing the highways to return to the government earlier.
ALR was established as a private, not-for-profit holding company to acquire the four concessionaires.
In October 2022, it issued RM5.5 billion in sukuk to finance the acquisition and refinance existing debt.
The SMART concessionaire, Syarikat Mengurus Air Banjir dan Terowong Sdn Bhd, became an ALR subsidiary.
ALR said it would not distribute dividends to shareholders, with revenue instead used to cover operating and maintenance costs and repay financing obligations.
The model was designed to maintain existing toll rates without government compensation under the restructured concessions, while directing funds towards debt repayment and an earlier return of the highways to the government.
The restructuring changed the financial and concession arrangements, not the tunnel’s flood-control function.
Who operates the tunnel now, and what happens next?
The SMART Tunnel concession is held by Syarikat Mengurus Air Banjir dan Terowong Sdn Bhd, which is wholly owned by ALR.
ALR aims to return all four highway concessions to the government by 2033, five years before the sukuk programme’s final maturity in 2038.
The return would not automatically make the highways toll-free. The government would decide on future toll arrangements, including whether to remove tolls or retain nominal charges to cover maintenance.

Title: Malaysia’s latest haze cost RM8b in welfare losses, may have led to 1,700 deaths, report finds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Malaysia’s recent haze episode carried an estimated RM8 billion in welfare losses, while short-term exposure to fine particles from fires may have contributed to about 1,700 deaths, according to a report commissioned by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM).
The report valued the health burden of estimated premature deaths at between RM3 billion and RM15 billion, using standard benefit-transfer methods.
It said this represents what people would be willing to pay to avoid the risk of premature death — not lost economic output — and should not be added to other economic losses.
The haze also disrupted manufacturers indirectly through staff absences and school closures.
Among 59 sites reporting some operational impact in FMM’s survey, 81 per cent said they experienced more sick leave or health-related absence, while 63 per cent said school closures affected staff availability.
The report also highlighted that, at 14 per cent of affected sites, staff shortages disrupted shifts, production or deliveries.
Overall, 37 per cent of sites reporting an impact said output fell, and 27 per cent temporarily shut down at least one operation.
The survey received responses from 86 FMM member sites, including 81 manufacturers.
More than two-thirds reported some operational impact, while 26 per cent said disruption was moderate or significant. The report cautioned that the survey was not representative of all manufacturers; most responses came from Selangor and Penang, and only two came from Sarawak.
School closures during the haze affected an estimated 8.4 million to 13.4 million student-days, the report said. It did not assign a monetary value to any loss in teaching quality.
FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said the haze should no longer be viewed exclusively as an environmental issue but also a matter of public health, labour productivity, economic sustainability and regional competitiveness.
“Manufacturing industries are increasingly interconnected through regional and global supply chains. Environmental disruptions in one country can affect economic activities and business operations across national boundaries.
“Preventing haze is therefore not only an environmental responsibility but also an investment in economic resilience, sustainable industrial development and the wellbeing of future generations,” he added.
The report also estimated 1,700 deaths related to the haze, with a 95 per cent interval of about 1,300 to 2,300, which covers the period from July 1 to Oct 22.
About 1,600 were attributed to smoke from fires outside Malaysia, the report said.
The report stressed that the figures are statistical estimates of deaths brought forward across the population, not individually identified cases.
If fire smoke is assumed to be no more toxic than other fine particles, the estimated toll falls to about 600.
The main estimate also carries uncertainty because the health-risk study used did not include Malaysian cities and was based mostly on forest fires rather than peat fires.
The research paper, titled “The 2026 Fire Season and Transboundary Haze in Malaysia,” covers the period from 1 July to 22 October 2026. It draws on satellite observations, air-quality monitoring, atmospheric modelling and findings from FMM’s member survey to assess the sources, severity and consequences of prolonged haze exposure.
The study was undertaken by Piyu Ke, Chief Scientist of Carbon Spur Sdn Bhd.
The study combined multiple scientific approaches to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the haze problem, including the cumulative effects of prolonged pollution exposure rather than focusing solely on peak air pollution readings.

Title: FMM report: Haze cost some Malaysian firms about RM280,000 in masks, medical expenses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The recent haze has cost some Malaysian businesses additional haze-related expenses of at least RM280,000, according to a report commissioned by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM).
The report said 45 sites provided estimates of extra spending in FMM’s survey of 86 member sites, 81 of them manufacturers.
Almost all respondents who reported an operational impact said they had incurred additional costs, mainly for masks and medical expenses.
Among the 59 sites reporting some impact, 92 per cent said they had spent more.
Masks were cited by 76 per cent and medical costs by 58 per cent, the report said.
The survey covered the effects of haze from October 5 onwards, with responses collected between October 12 and 21.
More than two-thirds of all responding sites reported some operational impact, while 26 per cent said disruption was moderate or significant.
FMM said the survey results describe only the responding sites and should not be treated as representative of all manufacturers.
Most respondents were in Selangor and Penang, and only two were in Sarawak, which the report identified as the worst-affected state.
The report also noted that extra spending across the wider economy, including on protection, was not valued because public data for this season were unavailable.
FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said that transboundary haze has become a recurring regional challenge that requires more decisive and coordinated action.
“Year after year, Malaysia and neighbouring countries continue to experience the consequences of transboundary haze. Beyond environmental degradation, haze affects people’s health, workers’ wellbeing, industrial productivity and economic activities.
“For manufacturers, prolonged haze can result in employee illness, absenteeism, disruptions to production and deliveries, and additional expenditure on protective measures and healthcare. These costs ultimately affect business competitiveness and economic resilience,” he added.
The federation urged regional leaders to give greater attention to transboundary haze pollution at the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meetings and Asean meetings, including through the relevant environmental, economic and ministerial cooperation mechanisms.
“Transboundary haze does not recognise national boundaries. Its consequences are shared by neighbouring countries, their populations and their economies. Therefore, its prevention cannot be the responsibility of any single country alone.
“FMM appeals to Apec and Asean leaders to place greater emphasis on this recurring challenge and strengthen regional cooperation in scientific research, environmental monitoring, early warning systems, sustainable land management and fire prevention,” said Lee.
According to the report, Malaysia recorded 422 city-days with an API above 100 across 13 cities between July 1 and October 22, compared with 207 in the same period of 2019.
West Sarawak experienced 63 days of haze episodes.
School closures during the season amounted to an estimated 8.4 million to 13.4 million student-days.

Title: Appeal court imposes 20-year sentence on headmaster for child sex offences
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — The Court of Appeal today sentenced a headmaster to 20 years in jail and 11 strokes of the cane for making pornography and committing physical sexual assault against a standard six student five years ago.
A three-judge panel, chaired by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin alongside Justices Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, dismissed Anuar Kintan’s appeal against his conviction and sentence of nine years and eight strokes of the cane imposed by the High Court for the charge of making pornography.
The panel, however, allowed the prosecution’s appeal to overturn the lower court’s decisions to acquit and discharge Anuar on the second charge of physical sexual assault against the victim, who was 12 years old at the time.
The court subsequently convicted him of the charge, sentencing him to 11 years with three strokes of the cane.
Justice Noorin, who delivered the unanimous decision, ordered the sentences to be served consecutively. She also issued a warrant of committal for Anuar, 59, to begin his sentence today. He had previously obtained a stay of execution of the sentence and was released on bail of RM14,000 with one surety pending disposal of his appeal.
The court, meanwhile, upheld the lower court’s decision to acquit and discharge Anuar on the third and fourth charges, which involved physical sexual assault on the girl and uttering words intended to be heard by the victim for sexual purposes.
Justice Noorin said the victim had given direct testimony identifying the accused as the person who took the photographs, and that her testimony had been considered by the Sessions Court judge who accepted it.
She said the existence of the photographs was not an isolated circumstance, but was supported by forensic examination that identified the images in Anuar’s Realme mobile phone.
On the second charge, Justice Noorin said the court disagreed that the alibi evidence presented by Anuar had raised reasonable doubt.
The defence had put forward an alibi in which Anuar’s wife testified that he was at home with her, and not at the school, when the incident occurred.
Justice Noorin said the testimony of the victim’s friend provided material support for the prosecution’s case regarding the accused’s presence at the school on April 3, 2021, and his movements with the victim. Therefore, the alibi evidence presented by the accused did not raise reasonable doubt.
On April 19, 2024, the Sessions Court found Anuar guilty of the first offence for making pornography by taking photos of the victim and sentenced him to three years in jail and two strokes of the cane.
The Sessions Court also sentenced him to an additional one year’s imprisonment and two strokes of the cane under Section 16 (1) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. The section provides for punishment if an offender commits a sexual crime while holding a position of trust over a child. The sentences were to run consecutively.
The Sessions Court, however, acquitted him of the second, third and fourth charges.
The High Court on Aug 15 last year increased the prison sentence for the first charge to nine years’ imprisonment and eight strokes of the cane and upheld his acquittal for the other three charges.
The offences were committed at a school in Perak in the middle of March 2021 and on April 3, 2021.
At the proceedings today, Anuar was represented by lawyer Amir Khusyairi Mohamad Tanusi while Deputy Public Prosecutors Azlina Mahmod and P. Sarulatha appeared for the prosecution. — Bernama

Title: PM says Budget 2027 reinforces Islam, criticises ‘hypocrite’ accusation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that Budget 2027 was formulated to continue promoting Islam, including through specific measures to strengthen pondok religious schools nationwide.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government had sought the views of Islamic scholars and religious teachers in drawing up the budget to ensure that the development needs of Islam received due attention.
He therefore criticised certain quarters for labelling the leader behind the Madani Government’s Budget 2027 as a “hypocrite”.
“When formulating Budget 2027, we asked what more could be done for Islam and what else could be added. In the past, we neglected pondok institutions and pesantren (Islamic boarding schools), but now we are rebuilding them.
“In the past, we sidelined the syeikhs, religious teachers and tuan-tuan guru (respected religious scholars), but now we invite them and seek their views,” he said when speaking at the Majlis Ilmu MADANI programme at Kompleks Seri Perdana here today, which featured renowned Indonesian preacher Ustaz Dr Abdul Somad Batubara as a guest.
Also present were the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail; Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan; and Weststar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim.
Anwar admitted that he was somewhat angered by the matter but said he remained patient, describing it as a systemic problem.
“When the matter was debated in Parliament, he called the leader a hypocrite and the budget hypocritical. If I were to ask Ustaz Abdul Somad, he would say, ‘Be patient, Pak.’ My heart was boiling, but I remained patient and did not respond.
“I just want to say that this is merely symptomatic of the real problem … those who profess Islam do not help or set a good example in terms of morals, personal conduct, moderation and tolerance,” he said.
Previously, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul had directed Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) to withdraw the word “hypocrite” that he had used during the debate.
The Prime Minister also expressed his appreciation to Abdul Somad for sharing his knowledge at the programme, adding that the preacher’s advice was always taken seriously in efforts to make Malaysia a better country.
“Ustaz Abdul Somad is now a prominent figure, but he is also controversial in some respects because he is bold in his criticism, which can sometimes be sharp.
“His criticism reaches all those in power, including in Malaysia. However, based on our experience in matters of governance and procedures, we welcome such criticism and try to make improvements,” he said.

Title: High Court dismisses ex-Axis adviser’s appeal, upholds jail term and RM800,000 fine
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The High Court here today dismissed the appeal by former Axis Incorporation Bhd board adviser Lee Koon Huat against his conviction and sentence on four charges of abetting the furnishing of false financial statements to Bursa Malaysia.
In a statement today, the Securities Commission (SC) said Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin held that the prosecution had proven the charges against Lee beyond reasonable doubt at trial and there were no grounds to interfere with the Sessions Court’s decision.
“The High Court further agreed with the SC’s submission that the sentence imposed against Lee was appropriate in view of Lee’s role in the commission of the offences.
“As such, the court dismissed Lee’s appeal against sentence and upheld the sentence imposed by the Sessions Court, being six months’ imprisonment and a fine of RM200,000 for each charge or in default, six months’ imprisonment,” it said.
The statement said, the court allowed Lee’s application for stay of execution in respect of the sentence of imprisonment, but declined to grant a stay in respect of the fine.
“Lee will have to pay a total fine of RM800,000 by today, failing which he will be imprisoned in default of the payment,” said the statement.
The SC said Lee was initially charged at the Sessions Court on 23 March 2013 with four charges under Section 122C(c) read together with Section 122B(a)(bb) of the Securities Industry Act 1983 (SIA) for abetting Axis in the furnishing of false financial statements relating to the revenue of Axis for the financial year 2007.
“Evidence adduced during the trial established that Lee had instructed the inflation of Axis’ reported revenue in its four unaudited quarterly results for the financial year 2007,” it said.
The SC had also previously charged three former Axis executive directors, Lee Han Boon, Saipuddin Lim Abdullah and Koh Tee Jin, with offences relating to the furnishing of false financial statements for the 2007 and 2008 financial years.
All three pleaded guilty and were sentenced to imprisonment terms ranging from one day to 12 months, while Lee Han Boon and Koh were also sentenced to fine of RM200,000 respectively.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Shoba Venu Gobal and prosecuting officers Low Wen Zhen, Eunice Ong, and Amina Qistina Mohd Idris appeared for the SC while Lee was represented by counsel Jason Ng Kau and Caroline Lee. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Dialogue with Myanmar offers best hope for Rohingya solution
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia has opted for diplomacy in dealing with the refugee issue involving Myanmar, despite facing international criticism over the government’s approach to resolving the matter, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the approach was necessary to seek a solution after years of criticism and condemnation directed at Myanmar had failed to bring about any significant change in the country’s policies.
“When I invited Myanmar President (Min Aung Hlaing), what was the objective? In my two previous meetings with him, I urged him to moderate his stance. We have been expressing anger and criticising them for 20 or 30 years, but it has had no effect. There has been no change in policy.
“The people in Rakhine, the Rohingya, continue to suffer. Some 200,000 have fled here, placing a burden on us as well. The people, including the Malay community, are becoming increasingly upset over the situation
Anwar was speaking at the ‘Majlis Ilmu Madani’ programme at Kompleks Seri Perdana here today, featuring prominent Indonesian preacher Ustaz Dr Abdul Somad Batubara as a guest.
He was explaining Malaysia’s position on refugees from Myanmar, including the Rohingya, and efforts to facilitate their return to their country of origin. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Malaysia must embrace AI, quantum technology without losing cultural roots
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia must continue to master emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing, to remain competitive globally while preserving its religious and cultural identity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said technological advancement was essential to ensuring the country kept pace with global developments, but must be anchored in religious faith, moral values, culture and literature.
“If we fail to master technology, others will overwhelm us. That is the principle. In the past, we fell behind because others mastered technology while we did not.
“But reaching for the sky must go hand in hand with being rooted in the ground. And what keeps us rooted? Our faith, morals, values, culture and literature,” he said.
He was speaking at the ‘Majlis Ilmu Madani’ programme at Kompleks Seri Perdana here today, featuring prominent Indonesian preacher Ustaz Dr Abdul Somad Batubara as a guest.
Also present were Anwar’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, and Westar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim.
Anwar said the culture of seeking knowledge must be strengthened to address the tendency among some individuals to raise problems without offering solutions based on knowledge and rational thinking.
He said a lack of in-depth understanding across various fields, including religion, could lead to tensions when people pass judgment on issues without sufficient knowledge or careful consideration.
“Even today, some religious teachers create problems. They learn a little about religion and immediately pass judgment, becoming ‘takfiris’ who declare others apostates or accuse them of hypocrisy,” he said.
Takfir refers to the practice of one Muslim declaring another Muslim an infidel or apostate.
He said the government would continue to strengthen religious education institutions, including traditional religious learning and the study of turath, or the Islamic intellectual heritage.
Anwar said the government also organised the monthly Madani Scholars Forum for senior leadership, including Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, to encourage informed discussion on such issues.
